jobs.title: Wireless Software Engineer (Starlink)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.
WIRELESS SOFTWARE ENGINEER (STARLINK)
At SpaceX, we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.
As a Wireless Software Engineer on these programs, you will be solving a wide range of novel engineering challenges:
- Firmware, embedded, and signal processing software running on custom hardware that flies the world’s largest fleet of spacecraft.
- Cutting-edge networking algorithms capable of connecting thousands of satellites to millions of users in real time.
- Infrastructure and tools enabling a highly reliable, software-defined global network.
Our Software Engineers are responsible for the complete lifecycle of the software they create, including development, testing, and support.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
- Design, implement, test, and maintain physical and MAC layer software of the wireless software stack for the Starlink communications network.
- Participate in architecting current and next-gen Starlink hardware and signal processing algorithms.
- Participate in hardware bring-up, debugging, verification and launch.
- Work with other teams for cross-layer integration of the end-to-end system.
- Develop prototypes to prove out key design concepts and quantify technical constraints.
- Collaborate with other engineers to plan and organize the development of our products.
BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
- Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, math, or STEM discipline; OR 2+ years of professional software engineering experience, programming with C or C++ in lieu of a degree.
- Experience working with wireless software or network protocols.
PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:
- Strong knowledge of wireless communications, signal processing and/or network protocols.
- Knowledge of RF systems and fundamentals: noise figure, link budget, non-linearity.
- Experience writing software for RF/mixed-signal integrated circuits and/or systems, such as phase-locked loops, mixers, data-converters, RF attenuators.
- Familiar with design and implementation of Digital Signal Processing algorithms and techniques: FFT, time and frequency domain equalizer, channel estimation, pilot tracking, digital pre-distortion, doppler compensation.
- Experience with lab equipment such as RF spectrum analyzer, network analyzer, signal generator, oscilloscope.
- Experience in any of physical and/or MAC layers in broadband access technologies such as: Wi-Fi, LTE, 5G or satellite broadband.
- Creative approach to problem solving, exceptional analytical skills and engineering fundamentals.
- Strong skills in debugging, performance optimization, and unit testing.
- Excellent communication skills both written and verbal.
- Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements.
ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
- Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed.
COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:
Pay range:

You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees in Washington State accrue paid sick time in compliance with state and federal law. jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern, BS/MS, Software Engineer, Multiverse
jobs.description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.
Software Engineering builds the brains of Waymo's fully autonomous driving technology. Our software allows the Waymo Driver to perceive the world around it, make the right decision for every situation, and deliver people safely to their destinations. We think deeply and solve complex technical challenges in areas like robotics, perception, decision-making and deep learning, while collaborating with hardware and systems engineers. If you’re a software engineer or researcher who’s curious and passionate about Level 4 autonomous driving, we'd like to meet you.
Waymo interns partner with leaders in the industry on projects that create impact to the company. We believe learning is a two-way street: applying your knowledge while providing you with opportunities to expand your skill-set. Interns are an important part of our culture and our recruiting pipeline. Join us at Waymo for a fun and rewarding internship!
You will:
- Contribute to the infrastructure to administer a “virtual driver’s test” for the Waymo Driver. Implement a project for our scalable simulation data pipelines that evaluate the driving capability of the Waymo Driver
- Apply software engineering best practices in order to improve code health and/or developer experience in the virtual driver’s test
You have:
- Currently pursuing Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related technical field
- C/C++ proficiency
- Strong verbal and written communication skills
- Excited about autonomous driving, eager to learn
We prefer:
- SQL skills
- Python programming skills
- Familiarity with distributed systems
- Comfortable with AI-assisted development features and workflows
Note: This will be a hybrid onsite internship position. We will accept resumes on a rolling basis until the role is filled. To be in consideration for multiple roles, you will need to apply to each one individually - please apply to the top 3 roles you are interested in.

We are moving beyond traditional perception to true scene understanding and driving actions—building offboard models that can comprehend complex driving problems, predict object/scene dynamics, and deduce driving paths with logical rationale.
Our core focus is advancing the VLM foundation itself. By pushing the boundaries of multimodal pre-training and state-of-the-art post-training (SFT, RL), we are creating models capable of rich, reasoning-based autolabeling at a massive scale. This closed-loop data engine directly powers the training and evolution of Waymo's real-time onboard models. If you are passionate about defining VLM training recipes, scaling laws, and unlocking complex reasoning via RL, this is your opportunity to redefine the foundation of autonomous driving.
In this hybrid role, you will report to a Senior Staff Technical Lead Manager.

- Drive Pre-training & Domain Adaptation: Lead the technical strategy for curating and constructing massive-scale, high-quality multimodal pre-training datasets. Define data mixture strategies to instill deep, Waymo-specific driving intuition and physics-grounded understanding into foundation models without catastrophic forgetting.
- Lead Post-Training & Reasoning Enhancement: Design and implement state-of-the-art fine-tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RLHF/RLAIF, DPO/GRPO/PPO) pipelines. Drastically improve the model’s instruction-following and complex reasoning capabilities (e.g., Chain-of-Thought, spatial-temporal reasoning, and driving rationale prediction).
- Pioneer the VLM Data Flywheel: Architect the highly scalable inference and evaluation pipelines that leverage these trained Gemini-class models to autonomously source, sample, and autolabel critical edge cases, directly accelerating the onboard perception models.
- Define Training Recipes & Scaling Laws: Conduct rigorous ablation studies to optimize model architectures, token budgets, and loss functions. Establish best practices for scaling multimodal training efficiently on large GPU/TPU clusters.
- Drive Cross-Functional AI Strategy: Act as the principal technical visionary across ML Infra, Perception, Behavior, and AI Foundation teams. Drive consensus on the data flywheel architecture and embed VLM reasoning capabilities seamlessly into the broader autonomous vehicle stack.
- Provide Staff-Level Technical Leadership: Own the long-term technical roadmap for foundation model development. Mentor senior engineers, lead rigorous design reviews, and establish standard-setting engineering practices from advanced prototyping to production deployment.
You Have:
- Master’s degree in Computer Science, AI, ML, or a related technical field.
- 8+ years of hands-on experience designing, training, and scaling deep learning models, with at least 3+ years focused deeply on training Large Language Models (LLMs) or Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
- Proven expertise in the full lifecycle of Foundation Models: from pre-training data curation (interleaved formats, tokenization) and distributed training to advanced post-training techniques.
- Expert-level understanding of training infrastructure and distributed paradigms (e.g., FSDP, Megatron, JAX/Pax) required for training massive models reliably.
- Expert-level software engineering fundamentals using Python, PyTorch, or JAX, with a track record of building reliable, highly scalable ML systems.
- Proven ability to operate with high ambiguity, define technical roadmaps, and drive complex, multi-quarter technical initiatives across multiple teams in a fast-paced environment.
We Prefer:

- Strong publication record in top-tier AI venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR) focusing on foundation models, large-scale training, reinforcement learning, or reasoning.
- Deep experience with advanced Reinforcement Learning paradigms applied to language or vision tasks (focusing on improving System 2 thinking, logical deduction, and model alignment).

jobs.description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.
The Simulator Team at Waymo builds state-of-the-art simulations of realistic environments for testing, training, and validation of the Waymo Driver. Our team is a multidisciplinary group of machine learning (ML) engineers, software engineers, and research scientists pushing the boundaries of autonomous systems. We develop industry-leading simulation platforms using large-scale generative and physical world modeling algorithms to model the physical world—encompassing dynamic agents, complex road topologies, multi-modal traffic systems, weather phenomena, and the vehicle’s full sensor suite (Camera, Lidar, Radar).
To pioneer the next frontier of fidelity, scalability, and physical controllability, we are expanding our focus on foundation world models. In this role, you will define and drive the technical roadmap for large-scale generative architectures, bridging cutting-edge multimodal pre-training (across 4D video, LiDAR, and Radar), spatiotemporal tokenization, and causal post-training/distillation to generate interactive, multi-platform, safety-critical driving worlds for closed-loop evaluation and onboard model training.
In this role, you will report to a Senior Staff Engineering Manager
You Will:
- Own the Architectural Roadmap: Drive the technical vision and long-term roadmap for foundational 4D world modeling, unified spatiotemporal tokenizers (3D/4D VAEs), video generation architectures, and generative sensor simulation across Waymo -- enabling zero-shot generalization across next-generation vehicle platforms, sensor rigs, and international geographies.
- Lead Large-Scale Pre-Training: Architect, train, and scale foundation video and physical world models (including Sparse MoE and long-context block-sparse attention architectures) across distributed TPU/GPU clusters, establishing efficient training recipes, multimodal data curation strategies, and scaling laws.
- Drive Advanced Post-Training & Alignment: Design and implement robust post-training paradigms, including Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), Reinforcement Learning with AI/Critic Feedback (RLAIF), model merging/souping, and 3D/semantic conditioning to guarantee strict physical realism, counterfactual pose-divergence stability, and fine-grained control over safety-critical scene elements (signage, traffic signals, VRU gestures, and adverse weather).
- Integrate Multimodal & Physical Signals: Develop action-conditioned, 3D-grounded physical world models and multi-view generative pipelines that couple explicit geometric and physical priors (4D scene graphs, occupancy, vehicle kinematics, and interactive agent dynamics) with neural synthesis across Camera, LiDAR, and Radar—faithfully modeling physical sensor transport, occlusions, and causal state transitions.
- Optimize for Production & Serving: Scale inference and evaluation frameworks into production simulation infrastructure, applying few-step and causal autoregressive distillation (e.g., Distribution Matching Distillation [DMD], Self-Forcing, Consistency/Flow distillation), quantization, and KV-cached streaming inference for 10 Hz high-throughput closed-loop validation and RL gyms.
- Foster Research-to-Production Impact: Partner closely with Onboard Perception, Planner, and AI Foundation labs across Waymo and Alphabet (e.g., Google DeepMind) to adapt frontier world models into deployment-ready simulation environments that achieve downstream perception/policy parity for rare-event reproduction, synthetic data training, and closed-loop RL.
- Mentor & Elevate Engineering: Serve as a technical authority, mentoring senior engineers and driving high engineering standards across training stability, reproducibility, and system design.
You Have:
- Education: PhD or MS in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, Computer Vision, or a related quantitative field (or equivalent practical research/industry tenure, including academic appointments looking to transition to industry).
- Senior Technical Leadership: 8+ years of industry or relevant research lab experience (or tenure-track/associate professorship equivalent) developing, deploying, and leading complex ML architectures.
- Large-Scale Pre-Training Track Record: Demonstrated experience training large-scale generative and physical world models from scratch (e.g., action-conditioned 3D/4D world models, large video diffusion models, autoregressive spatiotemporal transformers, flow matching, or vision-language-action models) on high-performance compute clusters (multi-node GPU/TPU).
- Post-Training & Alignment Expertise: Hands-on experience designing post-training and student-conversion pipelines for generative models—including few-step diffusion/flow distillation (e.g., DMD, MMD, Consistency Models, Rectified Flow), autoregressive exposure-bias mitigation (e.g., Self-Forcing), SFT, and Reinforcement Learning (RLAIF / reward-model alignment)—to control and stabilize long-horizon rollouts.
- Deep 3D/4D Vision Understanding: Deep technical foundation in 3D computer vision and physical world modeling—including action-conditioned scene dynamics, explicit 3D physical/geometric priors (4D occupancy, dynamic meshes, rigid/articulated kinematics), spatiotemporal tokenization (3D/4D causal VAEs), continuous ray/camera geometry (e.g., Plücker rays, cross-rig calibration), and generative 4D world representations (coupling explicit physical priors with neural generation).
- Framework Proficiency: Expert-level proficiency in Python and modern distributed ML frameworks (such as JAX/Flax, XLA/Pallas, PyTorch, Megatron-LM, Pathways, or DeepSpeed) for multi-node model, sequence, and data parallelism.
We Prefer:
- Domain Pedigree: Prior experience from leading video generation labs, foundation model startups, advanced robotics institutes, or high-tier academic research groups focusing on physical AI, foundation video models, or world simulation.
- Multi-Modal Sensor Simulation: Background in generative modeling and synthesis of non-RGB physical sensors—specifically 3D LiDAR point clouds/range images and 4D imaging radar—alongside multi-camera automotive rigs across diverse vehicle platforms, weather, and lighting conditions.
- Embodied AI & World Dynamics: Hands-on experience in physical world modeling and embodied dynamics—including action-conditioned causal world models, differentiable or hybrid physics engines, rigid/articulated body kinematics, vehicle dynamics, interactive multi-agent traffic dynamics, or closed-loop robotics simulators.
- High-Performance Infrastructure: Experience with low-level systems optimization, XLA/Pallas TPU kernels or custom CUDA/Triton kernels, block-sparse / Flash / Splash attention over 100k+ token sequences, and high-throughput KV-cached distributed serving.
- Systems Engineering: Working proficiency in modern C++ for high-performance simulation integration.

jobs.title: Embedded Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Who We Are
Nuro believes self-driving vehicles are the most immediate and profound opportunity for AI to drive positive change in the physical world. Safer streets, more time for what matters, and easier access to the world around us, that’s why we’re building a universal autonomy platform: self-driving for all roads and all rides.
Founded in 2016, Nuro is a physical AI company developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology for a wide range of vehicles, use cases, and markets. Powered by the Nuro Driver™, our universal autonomy platform enables the global mobility ecosystem to deploy autonomy at scale, from robotaxis and logistics fleets to personal vehicles.
With years of real-world deployment experience and a flexible, partner-led business model, Nuro is working toward a future where millions of autonomous vehicles powered by our technology help make everyday life safer, easier, and more connected.
Nuro has raised over $2B in capital from Uber, NVIDIA, Google, Softbank, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, and other leading investors.
About the Role
Nuro operates real self-driving vehicles on public roads today — not a research platform, not ADAS. The Embedded Software Engineering team builds the software for the safety-critical embedded controllers that connect the Nuro Driver™ to the vehicle: the devices that command steering, braking, and propulsion, alongside other vehicle actuators, distribute and monitor power, monitor vehicle motion, and bring the vehicle to a safe state when something goes wrong.
As an Embedded Software Engineer, you will work across the full stack of multicore automotive microcontrollers from RTOS, drivers, and scheduler up through middleware and application components that talk to the vehicle, and help extend that stack as our hardware evolves. You will bring the Nuro Driver™ up on new vehicle platforms alongside OEM and supplier engineers, and see your code drive real vehicles on public roads. We're hiring across levels, from engineers with a couple years of embedded experience to those who've shipped a production automotive launch.
About the Work
- Design, implement and test embedded C software for safety-critical multicore automotive microcontrollers, spanning base software such as RTOS, device drivers, scheduling and bootloader, middleware such as inter-component messaging and end-to-end protection, and application components such as actuator interface, body controls, power management and fault management.
- Integrate the Nuro Driver™ with new vehicle platforms: define and implement CAN and Ethernet interfaces with OEM ECUs, adapt actuator and body-control interfaces, and validate them on bench and in vehicle.
- Take part in hands-on device and vehicle bring-up, prototyping and debugging on multiple vehicle platforms, from first power-on to autonomous driving.
- Build and maintain the team's verification infrastructure: unit tests, hardware-in-the-loop benches and vehicle test procedures.
- Work within an ISO 26262 development process: define software requirements from system safety requirements, then implement and verify them with full traceability.
- Collaborate daily with systems, safety, hardware, controls and autonomy engineers, and with OEM and supplier partners, from definition through verification.
About You
- B.S. or higher in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a closely related field.
- 2+ years of industry experience developing embedded software in C, including work on a real-time operating system.
- Solid computer science fundamentals: data structures, concurrency and algorithm design.
- Working knowledge of microcontroller internals and peripherals, with depth in at least one of device driver development, CAN or automotive Ethernet, bootloaders and software update, embedded security, or vehicle-level integration and test.
- Strong problem-solving and debugging skills, clear written and spoken communication, and a track record of working well with engineers from other disciplines.
- Comfortable at the bench with debug probes, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers and CAN tools. You enjoy finding out why hardware and software disagree.
Bonus Points
- 3+ years of embedded development in the automotive or autonomous vehicle industry, including a production launch.
- Hands-on functional safety experience with ISO 26262, or safety-critical development in another regulated industry such as DO-178C or IEC 62304.
- Experience with Infineon AURIX TC3xx, SafeRTOS or FreeRTOS, or AUTOSAR Classic base software such as MCAL and communication stacks.
- Vehicle network integration experience: DBC and ARXML, UDS diagnostics, E2E protection, time synchronization.
- Knowledge of vehicle functions, vehicle dynamics or control theory.
At Nuro, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package. For this position, the reasonably expected base pay range is between $145,830 and $219,000 for the level at which this job has been scoped. Your base pay will depend on several factors, including your experience, qualifications, education, location, and skills. In the event that you are considered for a different level, a higher or lower pay range would apply. This position is also eligible for an annual performance bonus, equity, and a competitive benefits package.

About the Role
Nuro leverages many different bench-top systems to evaluate and regression test different aspects of the software and hardware integration layer. This performance simulation platform includes systems
At Nuro, every autonomy code change, from ML model updates to radius of map around the robot to number of evaluated trajectories, must be validated for real-time performance on actual robot compute hardware before it reaches the road. You will own the infrastructure that makes this possible.
Our Performance Simulation Platform is a hybrid benchmarking system: physical bench-top rigs running production robot compute (NVIDIA Thor platform), orchestrated by cloud-native infrastructure (Kubernetes, GCP), automated data pipelines feeding performance metrics into BigQuery and Grafana, pre/post simulation magic, custom tracing and profiling tools, and much much more.
Engineers across the company rely on this platform daily to answer questions like:
- How will my new ML model affect contention on the GPU?
- How does a new data format impact onboard logging rate or network contention as more data might be flowing from through the system?
- How much memory should be allocated for this new module, and how does it fit into the overall system budget?
You'll be responsible for development, integration, and the evolution of this platform — from the bare-metal OS and networking layer through the job orchestration and CI/CD integration up to the data analysis and visualization layer. This is a high-ownership, high-autonomy role on a small team where your work directly gates the release velocity of the entire autonomy stack. You'll be the technical DRI for the platform — setting the roadmap, making architectural calls, representing the platform's needs to the leadership team, and ensuring the system scales through multiple hardware generations.
About the Work
- Benchmarking Infrastructure: Develop and maintain the job orchestration layer that schedules, executes, and validates autonomy performance benchmarks across a fleet of physical bench-top systems — integrated into CI/CD pipelines as merge-blocking and release-blocking quality gates.
- Platform Reliability & Observability: Build monitoring, alerting, and self-healing automation for the bench fleet. Proactively identify systemic risks — capacity bottlenecks, hardware degradation patterns, infrastructure single points of failure — before they become outages. Track utilization, failure rates, and capacity trends to ensure the platform scales ahead of organizational demand.
- Performance Data Pipelines: Design and build end-to-end data pipelines that capture fine-grained performance metrics (CPU/GPU utilization, memory bandwidth, E2E latency, scheduling jitter) from bench-top runs, process them at scale, and surface actionable insights through dashboards and automated regression detection.
- Statistical Analysis & Experimentation: Work with Data Science to develop rigorous experimentation methodology for performance results from non-deterministic autonomy workloads — including variance analysis, significance testing, and regression detection.
Bare-Metal & OS Platform: Guide the SRE team through the OS and system-level configuration of bench hardware — including Linux kernel tuning, boot infrastructure, networking, and hardware bring-up — ensuring the platform faithfully reproduces production robot compute behavior.
- Drive Platform & Allocation Strategy: Own the planning lifecycle for the benchmarking fleet across hardware generations. Partner with engineering and program leadership to negotiate hardware allocation, model utilization scenarios under real-world constraints, and present data-backed trade-off recommendations — balancing testing coverage, user throughput, cost, and SLA commitments against finite physical resources.
- Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Hardware Engineering, NPI (New Product Introduction), SRE (Site Reliability Engineering), Perception, Behavior, and Data Science teams to translate their performance analysis needs into robust, self-service infrastructure.
About You
- Experience: 3+ years of industry software engineering experience.
- Software Engineering: Strong proficiency in Python and working proficiency in C++. You write clean, testable, well-documented code and care about long-term maintainability.
- Data Engineering: Experience building data pipelines, ingestion, transformation, storage, and visualization. Familiarity with SQL and analytical workflows.
- Systems & Infrastructure: Deep comfort with Linux systems — you've configured kernels, debugged boot issues, written systemd units, or managed bare-metal infrastructure. You understand networking, storage, and compute at a level beyond "it just works."
- Technical Leadership: Experience setting technical vision and roadmap for a project or platform, driving alignment across multiple stakeholders. You've independently identified the cross-functional partners needed to unblock and deliver, and you've briefed senior engineering leadership on trade-offs and recommendations.
- AI-Native: You treat AI as a core part of your engineering workflow, not an occasional shortcut — you use agentic tooling (e.g., Claude Code) across the development lifecycle and you understand the boundaries of when AI output demands extra scrutiny versus when it accelerates you.
- Bias for Action: Comfortable operating in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where you need to balance long-term architecture with short-term delivery.
Bonus Points:
- Experience with performance engineering, especially around tooling integration (perf, Perfetto, pprof, eBPF, NVIDIA Nsight Systems, NVIDIA CUPTI).
- Experience in robotics or AV, particularly with NVIDIA DriveOS stack.

jobs.title: Embedded Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Zoox is looking for an embedded software engineer to build out simulation infrastructure for our firmware. Our firmware runs on many ECUs across the robot, including the components that drive, brake, steer, and monitor the vehicle's health. Today, most of that firmware depends on hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) benches, which are expensive, hard to scale, and slow to iterate on. You will build the simulation capabilities that let firmware run in virtualized, software-in-the-loop (SIL), and hybrid SIL/HIL environments, integrated with Zoox's core simulation platform and the pipelines the rest of the autonomy stack already uses.
You'll be one of the first engineers on a new embedded-focused simulation team within the Firmware organization: simulation infrastructure engineering, built by and for firmware. The work you do here will lay the groundwork for Firmware's adoption of Zoox's simulation and more advanced test platform infrastructure. It spans much of the embedded stack, from low-level BSPs, through middleware such as messaging, HALs, and OSALs, up to the application layer. You'll need to understand what embedded software optimizes for (determinism, timing, resource limits, hardware interfaces) and turn that into simulation infrastructure that firmware teams trust and adopt.
In this role, you will:
-
Build out simulation infrastructure for Zoox's embedded platforms, filling the gaps in Zoox's simulation stack that keep firmware from adopting it
-
Virtualize embedded platforms across the stack, from BSPs and HAL/OSAL layers to messaging middleware and peripherals, so firmware can run without target hardware
-
Develop and extend SIL environments that integrate firmware with Zoox's core simulation platform and pipelines
-
Support and evolve hybrid SIL/HIL test platforms that combine real hardware with simulated components
-
Partner with Zoox's simulation, HIL, and firmware feature teams to adapt existing firmware for simulation and reduce the Firmware org's reliance on HIL
Qualifications
-
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical/Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, or equivalent experience
-
1–3 years of experience developing simulation infrastructure or embedded software for real-time systems
-
Strong C/C++ and Python programming skills
-
Understanding of embedded fundamentals: RTOS concepts, interrupts and timing, memory-constrained systems, and hardware/peripheral interfaces
-
Experience building simulation, emulation, or virtualization environments for embedded systems (e.g., SIL, QEMU, Renode, hardware/peripheral models)
Bonus Qualifications
-
Experience with QNX, SafeRTOS, FreeRTOS, or similar embedded operating systems
-
Familiarity with automotive communication protocols (CAN, LIN, Ethernet) and how to model or bridge them in simulation
-
Hands-on experience with HIL systems or hybrid SIL/HIL test setups
Compensation
There are three major components to compensation for this position: salary, Amazon Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), and Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights. A sign-on bonus may be offered as part of the compensation package. Compensation will vary based on geographic location and level. Leveling, as well as positioning within a level, is determined by a range of factors, including, but not limited to, a candidate's relevant years of experience, domain knowledge, and interview performance. The salary range listed in this posting is representative of the range of levels Zoox is considering for this position.
Zoox also offers a comprehensive package of benefits including paid time off (e.g. sick leave, vacation, bereavement), unpaid time off, Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights, Amazon RSUs, health insurance, long-term care insurance, long-term and short-term disability insurance, and life insurance.

jobs.title: Embedded Software Engineer, Wireless Technologies
jobs.description:
As a Software Engineer on the Firmware team, you will own the software integration, performance, optimization, and debugging of our TCU (Telematics Control Unit). Managing a complex architecture that integrates third-party hardware with our autonomous vehicle platform, you will analyze diagnostics and log outputs across cellular networks, 4G/5G modems, internal software layers, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth. You will not only reactively troubleshoot complex field issues but also proactively architect and develop robust host-side connectivity software to handle cellular edge cases and vulnerabilities before they impact operations.
Your work will directly safeguard the safety, reliability, and scaling of the Zoox autonomous fleet. Robust, low-latency connectivity is fundamental to autonomous vehicle deployment, powering essential real-time cloud services, fleet management pipelines, and teleoperation capabilities. By ensuring our vehicles maintain seamless, high-performance connections under the most demanding real-world conditions, you will bridge the gap between cutting-edge hardware, cloud infrastructure, and test systems to enable Zoox to deliver the future of autonomous mobility.
You will leverage a profound understanding of how these stacks operate to define the architecture, utilize vendor interfaces, and debug complex cross-layer issues.

Contribute and Develop: Contribute to Zoox's firmware and cellular wireless connectivity stack (LTE/5G), developing and enhancing connectivity features across multiple generations of hardware.
-
Vendor Integration: Act as the primary technical expert working with cellular chipset vendors (e.g., Qualcomm) to integrate their proprietary firmware, SW stacks, and L1-L3 implementations into our custom embedded Linux platform.
-
Architecture Definition: Define, architect, and validate the critical software interfaces between the RF-baseband, the vendor's protocol stack (AP), and our host system, writing the host-side glue code (C/C++) needed for the Linux networking stack.
-
Prototyping: Prototype and evaluate next-generation wireless platforms for future Zoox products.
-
Telemetry and Analytics: Develop the telemetry and analytics platform enabling data collection, analysis, and visualization of data reported from the Zoox fleet.
-
Investigate and Solve: Investigate and root-cause issues reported by QA teams and customer feedback. Differentiate between host-side bugs and vendor firmware issues using your deep knowledge of cellular protocols.
-
Quality and Automation: Support test automation frameworks, collaborate with QA, manufacturing, and other software teams, and drive continuous improvements and best practices within the broader organization.
Qualifications
-
More than 10+ years of experience in embedded linux systems and cellular/wireless stack software/firmware development.
-

-

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, ML Performance Optimization
jobs.description:
Zoox is on a mission to reimagine transportation and build autonomous robotaxis from the ground up that are safe, reliable, clean, and enjoyable for everyone. With bidirectional driving capabilities and four-wheel steering, our vehicle allows us to maneuver through compact spaces and change directions without needing to reverse. We are at a critical inflection point as we scale our robotaxi deployment, and it is a great time to join Zoox and have a significant impact on executing our mission.
Our growing ML performance engineering leadership team is looking for an Engineering Manager, ML Performance Optimization. The centralized ML performance team at Zoox plays a crucial role in enabling innovations across all our ML research teams to develop and deploy models across our robotaxi and cloud infrastructure and to advance cutting-edge training and inference optimization techniques.
The Opportunity
We are working on many interesting challenges to enable rapid experimentation and scale our multi-modal Foundation models and RL infrastructure, and ensure these models run efficiently on our vehicles, meeting our latency targets. You will get to work across all ML teams within Zoox - Perception, Prediction, Planner, Simulation and our Advanced Hardware Engineering group, and have the opportunity to significantly push the boundaries of ML scaling and acceleration at Zoox.
You will lead a team of strong ML performance engineers and this team has many growth opportunities as we expand our geofences at U.S markets and venture into new ML domains. If you want to learn more about our ML Infrastructure, here is one of our past talks at re:Invent.
In this role, you will:
-
Vision: Develop and execute a strategic vision and roadmap for ML Training and Inference Performance Optimization, ensuring scalability, reliability, and performance to support autonomous driving.
-
Technical acumen: Lead the design, implementation, and operation of a robust and efficient ML platform to enable the training, validation, serving, optimization and monitoring of ML models.
-
ML Performance Optimization: Drive end-to-end performance optimization for large-scale model training and inference, including distributed training efficiency, GPU utilization, memory and communication optimization, model compression (quantization, pruning, distillation), and low-latency on-vehicle inference that meets strict real-time and compute budgets.
-
Hiring: Attract, hire, and inspire a diverse world-class engineering team, fostering a culture of innovation, collaboration, and excellence.
-
Partnership: Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, including ML researchers, software engineers, data engineers, and hardware engineers, to define requirements and align on architectural decisions.
-
Mentorship: Enable engineers on the team to grow their careers by providing the right opportunities and clear, timely feedback.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Software Core Connectivity
jobs.description:
Zoox is building the world's most advanced self-driving hardware and software solution, and nearly every part of it depends on moving data reliably. Sensor frames to perception, planner decisions to vehicle controls, telemetry to the cloud, and remote operator video back down again. All of it crosses process, host, and network boundaries under hard latency and reliability budgets, on a vehicle that has to keep working when a link degrades or a network gets congested.
The Software Core Connectivity team owns that data path end to end: in-vehicle messaging (pub/sub, RPC, inter-process and inter-host transport), the vehicle's internal network, and vehicle-to-cloud connectivity. It also owns the transport and serialization abstractions the rest of the software organization builds on. Every one of those paths crosses a team boundary, so the work happens alongside firmware, product security, simulation, manufacturing, and IT, and those partners rely on this team for transport and networking depth to achieve their goals. As the team leader you will own the roadmap and the release commitments, and you will spend a real share of your time in those partnerships.
In this role, you will:
-
Own the roadmap, staffing, and release commitments across the team's messaging, in-vehicle network, and cloud connectivity work.
-
Lead and grow a team of software engineers, run their performance and promotion cycles, and hire into the gaps.
-
Represent the team in cross-functional programs across firmware, product security, simulation, fleet operations, and infrastructure, and build the relationships that keep shared work moving.
-
Set the technical bar. Make the architecture calls stick, and make sure the abstractions the team ships are ones other teams want to build on.
-
Balance interrupt-driven reliability work against long-horizon architecture, and be explicit with partners about the tradeoff.

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in computer science, electrical / computer engineering, or equivalent experience.
- 9+ years of experience in software development, with 4+ years in a leadership role managing software engineers.
- Strong grounding in at least one of: networked distributed systems, pub/sub and RPC middleware, vehicle or embedded networking, or transport protocols. Enough depth to hold your own in a design review without needing to run it.
- Strong C++ programming experience with large code bases and technical dependencies.

jobs.title: Program Tooling & Analytics Developer
jobs.description:
The Program Management Office (PMO) at Zoox is responsible for driving cross-functional program planning and execution at the highest level. We partner with leaders across vehicle development, software engineering, manufacturing, fleet operations, and business functions to deliver the major corporate milestones on the path to launch, and beyond. The quality of those decisions depends on how fast the right evidence reaches the right people — and that is what this role builds.
As a Tooling contractor in PMO, you will build the internal web tools and dashboards that decisions get made on. Zoox generates an enormous amount of data — fleet and simulation logs, program and issue tracking, operational telemetry, map and route data — but very little of it arrives in a form a leader can act on. You will close that gap: pull from existing sources, model the data properly, and ship tools that answer real business questions, including geospatial tooling that scores and compares candidate service areas to inform where we deploy next.
The feedback loop is short. Your users sit in the same building, your tools will show up in program and executive reviews within weeks of shipping, and you will own a piece of the stack end to end rather than work a ticket queue.
In this Role, You Will...
-
Build and ship internal web tools and dashboards on top of existing Zoox data sources, owning them from prototype through the version leaders rely on.
-
Start from the decision, not the dataset — work with TPMs and engineering partners to turn a vague business question into a scoped tool, then iterate quickly on their feedback.
-
Design the data layer behind those tools — queries, transformations, and pipelines that keep them current without manual intervention.
-
Extend our geospatial tooling with new attributes, data sources, and visualizations that sharpen where and how we expand service.
-
Handle real-world data honestly — surface coverage gaps, flag low-confidence results, and make each tool's assumptions visible to the people acting on its output.
Requirements
- Able to work on-site at our Foster City, CA office.
-
Time commitment is flexible and agreed at offer — part-time alongside coursework or full-time both work. A minimum of six months is preferred for continuity.

Currently enrolled in, or recently completed, a BS or MS in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or a related quantitative field — or equivalent practical experience.
-
Demonstrated experience building web tools or dashboards end to end, through coursework, internships, research, or personal projects. We care more about what you have shipped than where.

jobs.title: Senior / Staff Machine Learning Engineer - Behavior Models for Road Users
jobs.description:
This role in the Offline Driving Intelligence team is responsible for developing/learning behavior models for road users such as cars, bicycles, and pedestrians. These agents populate Zoox's simulations and must be indistinguishable from real road users, yet fully controllable: promptable into the rare, adversarial, safety-critical behaviors we need to test against. This means the team’s models directly impact how fast Zoox can train, validate and ship its driving stack. Our team collaborates closely with Planner, Simulation and Validation teams to develop and validate our driving performance. As an ML Agents Machine Learning Engineer, you will work on the bleeding edge of the industry, developing novel machine learning pipelines and models to predict the behavior of other agents in the world and planning the best course of action for the ego vehicle.
In this role, you will...
-
Develop new deep learning models that use imitation learning and reinforcement learning to generate driving plans for human-like driving agents.
-
Work on novel techniques to estimate the quality of those driving plans along the dimensions of safety, progress, comfort and realism.
-
Build generative behavior models (e.g. autoregressive, diffusion) that are conditionable on scenario intent — "cut off the ego vehicle," "jaywalk here" — for targeted stress-testing.
-
Leverage our compute, infrastructure and large corpus of data to push boundaries of the field.
-
Develop metrics and tools to analyze errors and understand improvements of our systems.
-
Collaborate with engineers on Perception, Planning, Simulation, and Validation to solve the overall Autonomous Driving problem.
Qualifications
-
PhD degree in computer science or related field and 4+ years of relevant professional experience or master's degree and 7+ years of relevant professional experience
-
Experience in one of the following: Planning, Prediction, Reinforcement Learning, Imitation Learning, generative modeling (diffusion, autoregressive models)
-
Experience with training and deploying transformer-based model architectures
-
Experience with production Machine Learning pipelines: dataset creation, training frameworks, metrics pipelines
-
Fluency in Python ML frameworks and a basic understanding of C++

Experience with JAX

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist
jobs.description:
We are seeking a Senior Data Scientist to join our Perception Verification and Validation team. The team is responsible for verifying and validating the perception stack of our autonomous driving system by building the metrics, datasets, and analyses that tell us how perception performance translates into driving behavior. As a senior member of the team, you will own the evaluation strategy for major perception capabilities from start to finish, partnering with perception and ML engineers, systems and safety engineers, and autonomy leadership to decide what to measure, how to measure it with statistical rigor, and what the results mean for release decisions.
Your work will directly shape how Zoox safely and efficiently ships perception improvements to our fleet, connecting model-level performance to end-to-end system behavior. You will also help raise the bar for the team by mentoring other data scientists and setting technical direction for how we validate perception.
In this role, you will...
-
Lead the design of metrics and evaluation frameworks for new perception capabilities, partnering with perception engineers early in model development to define what "ready to ship" means and how it connects to end-to-end driving behavior.
-
Drive cross-team validation projects, bringing together perception, systems, safety, and autonomy stakeholders to build consensus on metrics, evaluation datasets, and release criteria.
-
Develop rigorous statistical methods for uncertainty quantification, error estimation, and error propagation (frequentist, bootstrap, and Bayesian) so teams know when changes in performance are real.
-
Build evaluation datasets and analyze large-scale, highly geospatial fleet and simulation data to uncover perception failure modes, then turn findings into clear recommendations for engineering and executive leadership.
-
Mentor and guide a small group of data scientists by defining tasks, reviewing their work, and raising the team's technical bar.
Requirements:
-
Master's degree with 7+ years of experience, or PhD with 3+ years of experience, in data science, applied science, or a related quantitative role (Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related field).
-
Expert proficiency with SQL and/or Spark (PySpark or Scala) and Python, with a track record of building production-quality analyses and pipelines on large-scale (terabyte+) distributed data.
-
Deep expertise in statistical modeling, inference, and decision making, including uncertainty quantification, and a history of connecting point and uncertainty estimates to high-stakes decisions.
-
Experience designing metrics and validating ML models, such as computer vision, sensor-based, or perception models, including discovering and measuring failure modes.
-
Demonstrated track record of leading technical projects across teams, mentoring other data scientists or engineers, and presenting results and recommendations to senior leadership.
Bonus Qualifications:
-
Experience with autonomous driving, robotics, or other safety-critical systems, including system-level verification and validation or simulation.
-
Experience analyzing geospatial data and/or working with embeddings (e.g., similarity search, representation learning).
-

jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning  Engineer - Perception 3D Segmentation
jobs.description:
The Perception team at Zoox is responsible for the robot’s understanding of the world, fusing data from Lidar, Radar, and Cameras to create a unified representation of the environment. Design and implement state-of-the-art multi-modal sensor fusion architectures (Lidar, Camera, Radar) to predict 3D occupancy, semantic segmentation, and flow .

Develop "vision-first" fusion strategies to enhance geometric understanding and reduce dependency on sparse sensor modalities .

Engineer temporal processing modules to improve the stability and consistency of predictions over time.

Optimize model architectures for real-time on-vehicle inference, balancing high-fidelity range extension with strict latency constraints .

Collaborate with downstream consumers (Tracking, Prediction, Planner) to refine geometric outputs, such as contours and free-space estimations, for complex maneuvering.

MS or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, or related field with 6+ years of industry experience.

Deep expertise in 3D Computer Vision and Deep Learning, specifically with voxel-based or BEV (Bird's Eye View) architectures.
-
Strong proficiency in Python and deep learning frameworks (PyTorch) for model training and design as well as some experience in C++ for model integration.
-
Experience with multi-sensor fusion (Lidar, Camera, Radar) and handling temporal data sequences.

Experience with occupancy networks, implicit representations (NeRF/Gaussian Splats), or scene flow estimation.

-
Experience optimizing models for TensorRT/CUDA to achieve low-latency inference.
-
Familiarity with sparse convolutions or query-based architectures for efficient 3D processing.

Experience with Vision Language Model, or multi-modal 3D foundation model, or World Model, or VLA.

-

jobs.title: Senior Staff/Principal Software Engineer - GPU System Software, Onboard Execution
jobs.description:
Zoox is building a purpose-built robotaxi from the ground up and running it on public roads today, with riders. Every perception, prediction, and planning decision runs on an onboard compute: a fixed-power, fixed-thermal, safety-critical, real-time system.
That makes GPU execution one of the most consequential engineering problems in the company. Each new model generation wants more compute. Each new vehicle generation needs to cost less, use less power, and stay safe. Closing that gap is not a kernel-tuning exercise. It takes an end-to-end technical vision for how the whole onboard AI workload is scheduled, shared, isolated, and sized across GPUs, and the authority to drive that vision across ML, autonomy, middleware, and hardware organizations.
You will join Zoox's Software Performance organization, which owns end-to-end performance of the onboard software stack: profiling and observability, GPU compute, and compute platform. You will work closely with Perception, Prediction, Planning, ML Infrastructure, and Hardware teams, and you will be a senior technical voice for onboard compute across the company.
We are looking for the technical leader who sets that vision. You will define how Zoox runs AI on the vehicle, and you will own the strategy for doing more with less compute on every vehicle we build next.
In this role, you will:
- Architect onboard GPU execution. Define how perception, prediction, and planning workloads share onboard GPUs, including scheduling, multi-tenancy, isolation, and deterministic latency under contention.
- Drive compute reduction. Own the multi-year roadmap to cut onboard compute per vehicle by setting latency and utilization budgets and landing the biggest levers across models, runtimes, middleware, and hardware in real releases.
- Shape hardware and platform direction. Guide next-generation compute decisions (GPU and SoC selection, topology, memory budgets) with workload models and performance projections that justify them, then lead performance bring-up of each new platform.
- Lead inference performance at scale. Set direction for the inference stack (TensorRT, CUDA, custom kernels, quantization) and partner with ML teams so models are designed for the hardware they ship on.
- Provide technical leadership. Lead and mentor senior engineers, align directors and VPs through design docs, and make the hard calls when performance, safety, and schedule conflict.
Qualifications
- BS in computer science, computer engineering, or related field and 10+ years in systems or performance engineering, including leading GPU or accelerator architecture across teams, or building and leading a performance engineering team.
- Deep CUDA platform (programming model, runtime, and driver) and NVIDIA GPU microarchitecture expertise (Ampere through Blackwell, Orin, Thor).
- Proven record setting technical direction and delivering large, measurable end-to-end gains in latency, utilization, or cost.
- Working knowledge of ML inference optimization (TensorRT, XLA, Triton, quantization, fusion) and expert C++ on Linux.
- Ability to align ML, systems, hardware, and leadership on a shared technical plan.
Bonus Qualifications
- Real-time or embedded GPU experience: autonomy, robotics, AR/VR, games, or HPC.
Production GPU multi-tenancy (MPS, MIG, priority streams).
New GPU architecture or platform bring-up, benchmarking methodology, or workload modeling and projections.

jobs.title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, Core Connectivity
jobs.description:
Zoox is building the world's most advanced self-driving hardware and software solution. Inside the vehicle, dozens of processes across several compute hosts exchange sensor data, perception output, planner decisions, and control commands many times a second. Every millisecond spent moving that data is a millisecond the vehicle doesn't have to react, so the transport has to be fast and predictable, and keep working when a process restarts or a host comes up late.
The Core Connectivity team owns how that data moves, and how fast: shared-memory IPC between processes, transport between hosts, serialization, the RPC and messaging patterns application teams build on, and time synchronization across hosts. Nearly every software team at Zoox builds on this layer, so you'll work closely with the teams that use it, and your work shows up directly in how the vehicle drives.
In this role, you will:
-
Design and build low-latency inter-process and inter-host transport in C++: zero-copy data paths, shared-memory buffers, and lock-free queues. Measure and drive down end-to-end latency and jitter as message volume grows.
-
Make the transport hold up when processes crash or restart, hosts start out of order, and networks drop or delay packets. Chase fleet and simulation issues to root cause and fix them in the design.
-
Build the pub/sub and RPC messaging APIs application teams build on, so they get the delivery, ordering, and latency guarantees they need without having to understand the transport underneath.
-
Evolve message schemas and the Protocol Buffers based serialization layer: schema evolution, compact encodings, and moving existing users onto new formats without breaking anyone.
-
Set technical direction for a part of the stack and lead designs that span several teams.
Qualifications
-
Bachelor's or Master's degree in computer science, electrical / computer engineering, or equivalent experience, and 7+ years of experience in software development.
-
Strong modern C++ on Linux, in large codebases with performance-critical paths.
-
A background in transport or networking software, such as messaging systems, network protocols, or communication between distributed systems.
-
Experience building low-latency systems, and a track record of measuring and reducing tail latency, using techniques such as zero-copy, shared memory, lock-free data structures, and cache-aware data layout.
-
Solid systems fundamentals: concurrency, memory management, process lifecycle, sockets and the Linux networking stack.
-
Bonus Qualifications
-
Hands-on experience with shared-memory IPC, pub/sub or RPC middleware such as DDS, ROS 2, or iceoryx, or serialization frameworks such as Protocol Buffers, nanopb, or FlatBuffers.
-
Experience with PTP (IEEE 1588) or other time synchronization across machines, or with UDP multicast, MTU and fragmentation behavior, or time-sensitive networking.
-
Robotics, automotive, aerospace, or another real-time or safety-relevant domain.

jobs.title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, ML Training Optimization
jobs.description:
Zoox is on a mission to reimagine transportation and build ground-up autonomous robotaxis that are safe, reliable, clean, and enjoyable for everyone. We’re still early in deploying on public roads, so this is a great time to join and have a significant impact. The ML Platform team enables innovation in large-scale Foundation models, VLMs, and VLAs to make autonomous driving as seamless as possible.
The Opportunity
Are you excited to own ML training optimization at Zoox and make the models that power autonomous driving train faster, cheaper, and at greater scale? You’ll set technical direction for distributed training, parallelism strategies, mixed-precision training, and RL on SOTA accelerators, especially for multi-modal VLA and VLM models. You’ll partner with all Autonomy teams (Perception, Prediction, Planner, Simulation, Collision Avoidance) and act as a force multiplier for our internal customers, while mentoring engineers and shaping the team’s roadmap as we expand into new ML domains. If you want to learn more about our stack behind autonomous driving, please look here. If you want to learn more about our ML Infrastructure, here is one of our past talks at re:Invent.
In this role, you will:
- Lead the design, implementation, and operation of training performance optimizations (data/tensor/pipeline parallelism, mixed precision, gradient checkpointing, GPU kernels) to scale VLM, VLA, and Foundation model training.
- Own the technical strategy and multi-quarter roadmap for RL framework and RL performance optimization for driving foundation models.
- Drive profiling and root-cause analysis of throughput bottlenecks across the compute, compiler, framework, and cluster-networking stack.
- Partner with ML researchers, data engineers, and hardware engineers to define requirements and make architectural decisions for large-scale training infrastructure.
- Build custom kernels and benchmarks that track and validate performance gains across the stack.
- Mentor engineers and raise the team’s technical bar through design reviews and best practices.

- 7+ years of total experience, including 4+ years on large-scale model training platforms, with a record of leading projects end to end.
- Deep experience with distributed training frameworks (Megatron-LM, TorchTitan) and efficiently utilizing GPU/accelerator clusters at scale.
- Experience with RL frameworks (Verl/MILES) and algorithms (GRPO, PPO).
- Experience with collective communication libraries (e.g., NCCL) and optimizing communication/compute overlap in multi-node training.
- Strong command of profiling tools (NVIDIA Nsight, PyTorch Profiler, or XLA/JAX profiling) to find and resolve training bottlenecks.
- Proficiency in Python or C++.

jobs.title: Software Engineer - Collision Avoidance System Metrics
jobs.description:
The Collision Avoidance System (CAS) is responsible for detecting and reacting to imminent collision situations in support of our vehicle’s overall safety goals. CAS Perception is responsible for processing raw sensor data from our vehicle’s world-class sensor suite using a combination of geometric, interpretable algorithms and deep learning to detect near-collisions with obstacles along our intended driving path, in the most challenging dense urban environments and under tight compute resource constraints. Overall CAS is parallel and complementary to our Main Artificial Intelligence (AI) autonomy stack, and has a close relationship with our vehicle hardware and safety teams in order to architect redundancy into our overall driving system.
The CAS Verification & Validation (CAS V&V) is a multidisciplinary team data, software and systems engineers defining and building metrics to measure the Collision Avoidance System performance and work with the Systems Design and Mission Assurance (SDMA) and QA teams to develop validation plans for the features.
In this role, you will:
- Apply distributed computing algorithms to analyze petabytes of urban driving data.
- Develop metrics and tools to analyze errors and system improvements.
- Work closely with CAS engineers to evaluate system performance.
- Collaborate with Perception engineers to define metrics for autonomous driving.
- Partner with Planning engineers to measure performance in complex urban environments.

- Extensive experience with programming and algorithm design

jobs.title: Staff / Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer - Collision Avoidance System
jobs.description:
The Collision Avoidance System (CAS) is Zoox's independent safety layer. It runs alongside our main autonomy stack, constantly watches for imminent collisions, and reacts within milliseconds to prevent or reduce them. By using different methods and data paths than the main stack, CAS gives our robotaxi a second, diverse line of defense in the most challenging dense urban environments.
As a Staff or Senior Staff engineer, you will be the technical lead for CAS algorithms, with a focus on CAS perception. You will shape how CAS sees the world, combining interpretable geometric methods with machine learning, and you will own the architecture and roadmap that take these capabilities from idea to safe, real-time deployment on our fleet. Your work will directly affect the safety of every rider and road user around our vehicles.
In this role, you will:
- Serve as the technical lead and architect for CAS perception, defining how lidar, radar, and camera data become reliable obstacle detection, tracking, and collision-risk estimates under tight latency and compute budgets
- Design, implement, and ship both machine learning and classical perception algorithms (e.g., point-cloud geometry, ground estimation, clustering, state estimation and tracking, learned detection and segmentation, sensor fusion) in production-quality, safety-critical C++
- Own the end-to-end CAS algorithm architecture and multi-release technical roadmap, making clear trade-offs between safety, performance, latency, compute, and ML vs. non-ML approaches
- Partner across CAS perception, behavior and planning, and validation to define interfaces, requirements, metrics, and evaluation strategies that show the system is safe and ready to launch
- Work with sensor, system performance, safety strategy, and main autonomy teams to drive cross-team technical decisions, while mentoring engineers and raising the technical bar across CAS
Qualifications
-
BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent experience
-
At least 10 years of experience developing perception or related algorithms for robotics, autonomous vehicles, or other real-time systems
-
Deep expertise in 3D perception from lidar, radar, and/or camera, with hands-on experience in both machine learning (detection, segmentation, fusion) and classical methods (geometry, state estimation, tracking)
-
Strong C++ or Python skills and a track record of shipping efficient, reliable real-time software to production
-
Experience leading the architecture and technical roadmap of a complex production system across multiple teams
Bonus Qualifications
-
Conference or Journal publications in Machine Learning or Robotics-related venues
-
Experience with safety-critical systems or functional safety practices (e.g., ISO 26262, SOTIF), collision avoidance, emergency braking, prediction, or planning systems for autonomous vehicles
-
Experience optimizing and deploying models or algorithms on onboard compute (e.g., GPU / CUDA, TensorRT)

jobs.title: Staff Network Security Architect
jobs.description:
Zoox's Network Security team architects and defends the digital borders of the company, from corporate offices to engineering labs and product/mission environments. As Staff Network Security Architect, you own the target-state design for how Zoox segments, connects, and controls trust across enterprise IT, OT and lab networks, and hybrid cloud (AWS, GCP). You set the standards other teams build to, you are the security design authority on new infrastructure, and you are accountable for the coherence of the whole picture rather than the health of any one platform. You'll partner closely with Network Engineering, IT, Product Security, Hardware, and Software Engineering, and you'll influence far more systems than you personally operate.
In This Role, You Will...
- Own Zoox's network security reference architecture across corporate, data center, lab/OT, and edge environments, and define the segmentation and trust model that everything else is built against
- Serve as the security design authority for new infrastructure: run design reviews and threat models early enough to change the design, and define the criteria under which a design is approved, conditionally approved, or rejected
- Translate security frameworks into buildable engineering standards. Map controls to NIST CSF 2.0, NIST 800-53, and ISO 27001 (IEC 62443 a plus for OT/lab), and turn them into reference patterns, guardrails, and acceptance criteria engineers can implement without interpreting policy
- Define the zero-trust and identity-to-network strategy, including 802.1X/certificate-based NAC, PKI trust hierarchy, ZTNA and remote access, and how non-human and headless lab/vehicle assets are authenticated and authorized
- Architect secure hybrid and multi-cloud connectivity (CloudWAN, SD-WAN, transit and inspection architectures, cloud-native controls) and define where inspection, enforcement, and logging belong
- Drive secure-by-design into the delivery path: encode standards as Terraform modules, policy-as-code, and CI/CD guardrails so the secure pattern is the default one, not a review gate
- Own data flow and trust boundary analysis for sensitive environments, including vehicle data, lab telemetry, and third-party and vendor connectivity
- Own the governance side of architecture: risk articulation for leadership, exception and compensating control decisions, architecture decision records, and the multi-year roadmap that retires legacy patterns
- Set technical direction and raise the bar across the team through mentorship, design review, and written standards rather than through direct ownership of day-to-day operations
Qualifications
- 10+ years in network and security engineering, including 4+ years in an architecture or technical-lead role where you owned designs others implemented
- Demonstrated ownership of an enterprise-scale segmentation or zero-trust architecture from concept through adoption, including what you changed when it met reality
- Ability to reason about security frameworks as design inputs, not audit artifacts: fluency with NIST CSF 2.0, NIST 800-53, and ISO 27001, and a track record of turning them into engineering standards and evidence
- Depth in threat modeling and secure-by-design for network and infrastructure, including data flow analysis, trust boundaries, blast radius, and failure modes
- Strong platform grounding to keep designs buildable: next-gen firewalls (Palo Alto, Fortinet), AWS NFW, IDS/IPS, NAC/802.1X, PKI, VPN, ZTNA (Zscaler, Prisma Access, or equivalent), and core protocols (TCP/IP, BGP, OSPF, VLAN, TLS/PKI)
- Cloud network security depth in AWS and/or GCP, including inspection architecture, cloud-native enforcement, and IaC delivery with Terraform
Bonus Qualifications
- OT, ICS, robotics, automotive, or manufacturing network security experience (IEC 62443, Purdue model, or equivalent)
- Autonomous vehicle or safety-critical systems exposure
- Certifications: CISSP-ISSAP, SABSA, TOGAF, CCIE Security, PCNSE, AWS Security Specialty
- Experience applying AI/ML to network or cloud security (anomaly detection, behavioral analytics, LLM-assisted design review or policy analysis)

jobs.title: Staff Systems Engineer, Simulation Systems Verification and Validation Lead
jobs.description:
Zoox is on an ambitious journey to develop a full-stack autonomous mobility solution for cities. Simulation lets us test our driving software against far more scenarios than we can drive on public roads. For simulation results to count toward our safety case, we must show how closely the simulator matches reality and how much uncertainty the remaining difference adds to our safety metrics.
We are seeking a Simulation Systems Verification and Validation (Sim VnV) Lead to own that work across the full autonomy stack. You will define how to validate simulation at the sensor, perception, planning, and full-pipeline levels, lead the cross-functional program that executes the sim VnV program, and turn the results into clear evidence about when and where simulated miles can support safety clearance decisions. You will work closely with simulation, perception, planning, hardware, safety, data science, and systems engineering teams. This is a highly visible, technical leadership role on the critical path to safely scaling our service.
The ideal candidate demonstrates systems thinking, can lead a complex program across teams, and knows how to validate a model of a closed-loop system that has an AI controller inside it.
In this role, you will:
-
Own the end-to-end simulation V&V strategy across different levels of integration ranging from sensors-only through the full system behavior for the purpose of constructing a safety case for fully autonomous driving on public roads.
-
Define the data sets, metrics, and comparison methods.
-
Lead a recurring cross-functional sim validation program with simulation, perception, planning, systems engineering, safety, and data infrastructure teams. Set milestones and cadence, track risks and dependencies, and drive decisions to closure.
-
Partner with statisticians and data scientists on estimators that combine simulated and real-world results into safety performance measures.
-
Write the methodology documents and validation reports, and present results, risks, and recommendations to engineering and executive leadership.
-
Mentor engineers across teams in V&V practice and systems thinking.
Qualifications
-
M.S. or higher in Systems, Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, or Robotics Engineering, Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics, or a related field.
-
8+ years of experience in verification and validation of safety-critical systems that contain software or autonomy (for example autonomous vehicles, ADAS, aerospace guidance and flight software, or robotics).
-
A record of leading technical programs across several teams, from an ambiguous problem statement to a delivered result.
-
Working-level experience validating a simulation or model against real-world data so that its results could support a decision, preferably for a closed-loop system with software or a learned controller in the loop.
-
Strong systems thinking: you can break a system into integration levels, define the interfaces and the evidence needed at each level, and connect component-level results to system-level claims.
-
Experience deriving or implementing estimators that fuse simulated and real data, for example control variates, prediction-powered inference, Bayesian hierarchical models or power priors, importance sampling, or rare-event estimation. Similar experience with modeling uncertainties and failure rates is also acceptable.

-
Experience with sensor simulation (camera, lidar, radar), neural rendering or generative scene synthesis, or perception evaluation metrics.
-
Experience evaluating motion planning or behavior in closed-loop simulation at scale.
-
Familiarity with model credibility and safety standards, such as NASA-STD-7009, ASME V&V 10/20/40, ISO 21448 (SOTIF), UL 4600, ISO 26262, or ISO 34502.
-
Hands-on Python and SQL.
-
Ph.D. in a relevant field.

You will leverage your substantial prior expertise in connectivity software and protocols (cellular modem cross-layers, Wi-Fi MAC/PHY) to provide critical insights and feedback, guaranteeing that our systems are rigorously tested and hardened for operational deployment.
In this role, you will:
-
Test Architecture & Strategy: Define component integration plans (from initial hardware bring-up to advanced functions), then design, develop, and execute comprehensive test plans spanning early development through large-scale operational fleet deployment.

Advanced Testing Campaigns: Proactively design and facilitate advanced testing campaigns utilizing industry-standard network emulation tools (e.g., Keysight UXM) to identify cellular edge cases, performance bottlenecks, and vulnerabilities.

Deep Debugging: Dig into challenging log reviews and cross-functional system integration mysteries to identify root causes. Propose solutions balancing long-term architectural goals with near-term operational needs.

Interface Validation: Ensure all interfaces are well-architected, documented, and rigorously validated—notably between RF-baseband, baseband-protocol stack (AP), and AP to host.

Automation & Frameworks: Develop and enhance log frameworks and automation scripts to analyze wireless communication behavior at scale.

B.S. or M.S. degree in Electrical Engineering, Telecommunications, Computer Science, or a similar discipline with 10+ years of industry experience in wireless validation or embedded systems test engineering.

- Take ownership of complex production issues in distributed SaaS environments, leading deep root-cause analysis and implementing permanent preventive safeguards.

- Write clean, maintainable, high-performance production code and build proof-of-concepts that settle architectural questions.
- Establish rigorous engineering standards through code reviews, automated testing, and CI/CD integration.
- Identify architectural bottlenecks and technical debt, and drive practical, iterative refactoring without compromising business delivery.
Security, Privacy & Compliance
- Ensure platform designs and team practices align with information security standards and regulatory requirements.
- Design for tenant isolation, access control, auditability, and data residency from the outset.
Technical Leadership
- Provide architectural guidance across multiple engineering teams.
- Lead architecture reviews, design discussions, and technical decision-making.
- Mentor senior and staff engineers, raising the bar through reference implementations and sponsorship rather than authority.
- Influence engineering strategy and long-term technology investments; articulate complex trade-offs to both technical panels and executive stakeholders.

- Proven experience designing and operating enterprise-scale, multi-tenant SaaS platforms, with real numbers for throughput, latency, availability, and behaviour under failure.
- Strong understanding of distributed systems fundamentals: consistency and idempotency, retries and backpressure, concurrency, caching, and database design and optimization.
- Demonstrated ownership of large-scale migrations or modernization initiatives with measurable outcomes.
- Advanced production debugging skills — Linux internals, profiling, log analysis, and telemetry in distributed cloud environments.
- Experience leading cross-functional architecture initiatives in SaaS or product organizations.
