Job Description
We are looking for a Principal Engineer — Product & Application Security to be the top technical authority for how Freshworks builds secure software. As an IC6 Principal, you set the multi-year security technical vision for our products and platform, make the calls on our hardest security-architecture problems, and are the person the company relies on when the stakes are highest — across a multi-tenant SaaS estate serving 72,000+ customer accounts and hundreds of integrations.
As Freshworks evolves from a suite of service products into an AI-first system of business intelligence — with autonomous agents, a Knowledge and Context Graph, and a growing agentic surface — the security bar must rise with it. This role goes beyond leading individual reviews and remediations: you define the secure-by-design paradigms, reference architectures, and organization-wide standards that determine how thousands of engineers ship, and you drive the strategic bets (AI/agent security, supply-chain integrity, zero-trust data protection) that keep Freshworks ahead of the threat curve.
You will operate as a company-wide force multiplier — writing code and reference implementations, setting technical direction that outlives any single project, mentoring Staff and Senior Staff security engineers, and partnering directly with VP Engineering, the CISO organization, and product leadership to make security a durable competitive advantage.
Key Responsibilities
Security Technical Vision & Strategy
- Own the multi-year technical vision and architecture strategy for product and application security across all Freshworks products (Freshdesk, Freshservice, and the shared Platform), and drive alignment on it across engineering and the CISO organization
- Define the secure-by-design reference architectures, paradigms, and organization-wide standards (authN/authZ, tenant isolation, data protection, secrets, API security) that thousands of engineers build against
- Set the strategic security agenda for the AI-first platform — securing the AI Agent Platform, Knowledge/Context Graph, and agentic workflows — anticipating threat classes before they reach production
- Act as the final technical decision-maker and tie-breaker on the hardest, highest-risk security-architecture trade-offs
Product & Application Security Engineering
- Lead threat modeling and security design reviews for the most critical, cross-cutting, and highest-risk systems — including identity and access, the integrations/connector framework (300+ apps), and the agent runtime
- Set the standard for secure code review, manual and AI-assisted penetration testing, and vulnerability analysis; drive root-cause remediation strategies that eliminate whole vulnerability classes across the estate, not one bug at a time
- Architect and harden multi-tenant security controls: strict tenant isolation, authentication/authorization models, secrets management, data protection, and API gateway security
- Own the security design for AI/agentic features — prompt injection defense, tool-invocation authorization, non-human identity, and permission-scoped context access
Left-Shift & Secure SDLC at Scale
- Define the organization-wide, AI-assisted left-shift strategy: how SAST, DAST (e.g., Snyk), SCA/dependency scanning, secret detection, and IaC scanning are embedded across every CI/CD pipeline to catch issues before production
- Set the direction for security tooling, automation, and paved-road frameworks and libraries that make the secure path the default path — including code-component asset inventory (API/SBOM/RBAC/secrets/integrations) and secure-by-default product hardening
- Own the software supply-chain security strategy: centralized software artifact repository management (e.g., Sonatype Nexus), code artifact repository guardrails, and CI/CD pipeline hardening
- Establish secure coding standards, golden patterns, and guardrails; operationalize threat modeling and maturity models (SAMM) across the product portfolio; and define the security quality gates the whole org is measured against
Vulnerability Management & Incident Response
- Serve as the top technical escalation point for the most severe security incidents — leading investigation, containment strategy, and post-incident architectural hardening
- Set the risk-based prioritization framework for findings from internal testing, bug bounty, third-party pen tests, and researcher disclosures, and drive systemic fixes
- Shape the strategy for the bug bounty and responsible-disclosure program
Technical Leadership & Influence
- Act as the recognized top IC authority for product security — mentoring and multiplying Staff and Senior Staff engineers and security champions, and raising the security bar across the entire engineering organization
- Influence company-level strategy: advise VP Engineering, the CISO organization, and product leadership; represent Freshworks' product-security posture to enterprise customers, auditors, and (where appropriate) the external security community
- Drive cross-organizational security initiatives to completion through technical credibility and clarity — building consensus across many teams without formal authority
Security Domains You'll Set Direction On
You will be expected to provide deep technical direction — and roll up your sleeves — across the full product security roadmap, including:
- Compliance & trust enablement: internal and external pen testing (PCI vault, VAPT), Google CASA, TX-RAMP control validation, SDLC documentation control reviews, audit evidence, risk assessment prioritization, and new-product-introduction (NPI) security assessments
- Continuous security assessment & automation: DAST onboarding for public APIs and continuous-deployment integration, SCA bug triage, CI/CD environment assessment, continuous control monitoring, security scorecards, and anomaly-detection rule configuration
- Shift-security-left: code-component asset inventory (API/SBOM/RBAC/secrets/integrations), supply-chain attack prevention, threat-modeling operationalization, and product-security maturity models (SAMM)
- Product security features: step-up authentication for sensitive operations, SCIM/secure SAML, OIDC federated SSO, OAuth for APIs and third-party apps, secrets injection, customer data masking, field-level encryption, BYOK, DNSSEC, header hardening (CSP/X-Frame), IMDSv2, egress proxy enforcement, hardcoded-secret cleanup, IAM role right-sizing, SIEM audit-log integration, and SSPM tool integration
Metrics & Impact
- Define the security KPIs the organization is held to: reduction in high/critical findings reaching production, coverage of critical services by threat models, mean time to remediate, and adoption of secure-by-default frameworks
- Deliver a measurable, sustained reduction in exploitable risk across the entire product portfolio while improving — not slowing — engineering velocity
Qualifications
Professional Experience
- 12+ years in software engineering and/or security, with deep, sustained hands-on ownership of application/product security for production SaaS at enterprise scale
- Track record as a Principal-level (or equivalent) individual contributor whose technical vision and standards shaped an entire engineering organization — you have defined direction that outlived individual projects
- Deep experience securing multi-tenant, cloud-native SaaS platforms (ideally on AWS), including tenant isolation, authN/authZ, and API security at scale
- Demonstrated impact eliminating vulnerability classes and setting the security frameworks, reference architectures, or paved roads adopted org-wide
Technical Expertise
- Authoritative, current knowledge of application security anchored in OWASP frameworks — Web Top 10, API Security Top 10, ASVS, the LLM Top 10, and the newer OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 (the real-world attack classes targeting autonomous agents) — plus secure design patterns, authentication/authorization (OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, SCIM), session management, and cryptography
- Mastery of threat modeling (e.g., STRIDE), secure code review, and both manual and AI-assisted penetration testing across web, API, and cloud surfaces
- Deep experience embedding security into CI/CD at scale: SAST, DAST (e.g., Snyk, Snyk Code), SCA, secret scanning, IaC scanning, artifact-repository management (e.g., Sonatype Nexus), and container/Kubernetes security aligned to the OWASP Kubernetes Top Ten (RBAC, workload isolation, supply-chain, and misconfiguration risks)
- Strong coding ability in one or more of Ruby, Java, Go, Python, or JavaScript/TypeScript — enough to build reference implementations and security tooling and to be credible in any code review
- Deep cloud security expertise (AWS preferred): IAM and role right-sizing, network/egress controls, KMS/secrets management, BYOK/field-level encryption, and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform/CloudFormation)
- Authoritative grasp of cryptographic and compliance standards relevant to enterprise SaaS — e.g., FIPS 140-2/140-3, PCI, SOC 2, ISO 27001, and Google CASA / TX-RAMP control frameworks
- Deep understanding of securing AI/LLM and agentic systems — including Claude and other LLM security concerns such as prompt injection, insecure tool use, model/data exposure, and non-human identity
Leadership & Influence
- Ability to set technical direction for and influence an entire engineering organization — and senior executives (VP/CISO) — through technical credibility and clear communication
- A genuine service-oriented, "make the secure path the easy path" mindset toward internal developers
- A multiplier: track record of growing Staff and Senior Staff engineers and building a durable security-champion culture across distributed teams
Nice to Have
- Deep experience securing ITSM, CX/CRM, or service-management products and their data models
- Recognized external contributions: open-source security projects, published research, CVEs, standards bodies, or conference talks (e.g., Black Hat, DEF CON, OWASP)
- Industry certifications such as OSCP, OSWE, GWAPT, CISSP, or equivalent (valued, not required)
- Experience defining or scaling bug bounty / responsible-disclosure programs
- Deep familiarity with modern AI/ML stacks — LLMs, embeddings, RAG pipelines, and agent frameworks (LangGraph, MCP, A2A) — and their security models
- Experience shaping compliance and audit programs (SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, GDPR)
Additional Information
Please note this is a hybrid role with onsite expectations of 3x/week (Tues - Thurs) from our San Mateo, CA headquarters.
The annual base salary range for this position is $241,000 - $298,000. This role is also eligible for a target bonus.

Join us on our mission to make a better world of work.

How you can help make a better world of work
The People and Systems Analyst is the analytical and technical backbone of the People Systems and Analytics function. You will act as an analytical partner to Total Rewards and the wider People function. You will report to the Manager, People Systems and Intelligence. You will support compensation analytics and modeling for Total Rewards. You will deliver people analytics across the function. You will understand People Systems (such as HRIS, ATS, LMS) within the People team's remit. You will design and build AI-powered workflows and automations to improve efficiency across the wider People function.
As part of this team of amazing humans,
You will:
- Build and maintain automated reports, dashboards, and self-serve analytics tools for the People function and business leaders.
- Support wider people function with activities like with salary band modeling, pay equity analysis, performance & compensation cycles, compliance reporting, and engagement, etc.
- Design and build automations for high-volume processes across People Operations and Compliance.
- Own People Systems configuration, data pipelines, and downstream integrations for the People team.
- Document systems architecture and maintain a prioritized backlog of automation opportunities.
You have:
- Experience in HR, people data, or business analytics.
- High proficiency in HRIS platforms, ideally BambooHR, including data models and workflow configuration.
- Strong data querying and modeling skills using SQL and Business Intelligence tools.
- Clear systems thinking skills with the ability to map processes and identify failure points.
- Practical experience with agentic AI frameworks.
- Excellent documentation habits to help others understand and maintain your work.
Nice to have:
- Hands-on experience building automated workflows using no-code tools or scripting languages.
You are:
- Able to understand data and create actionable insights
- Able to design automation for people processes
- An analytical partner to the whole people function and business
- Focused on providing technical delivery capability so leaders can focus on strategic insight.
Perks & Benefits
At Culture Amp, our people are at the heart of our success. We offer competitive pay and a total rewards package designed to support you at work and in life. This includes:
- Equity through our Employee Share Option Program, so you can share in our long-term success
- Learning programs and coaching to help you thrive and grow
- Quarterly refresh days, an extended end-of-year break and a monthly allowance to support your wellbeing and lifestyle
- Inclusive parental leave from day one
- A MacBook and budget to set up your home workspace, enabling flexibility
- Five annual social impact days to to give back to causes that matter to you
- Medical insurance coverage for you and your family (Available for US & UK only)
Our rewards are designed to support different needs and life stages, recognising that what matters most can vary from person to person.
Research shows that candidates from underrepresented backgrounds may hesitate to apply if they don’t meet every requirement, but your unique experience matters. If you’re interested in joining us, we strongly encourage you to apply and help us build a more diverse and impactful team.
Accommodations & Data Privacy
If you require reasonable accommodations or adjustments due to a disability to complete the online application or to participate in the interview process, please contact accommodations@cultureamp.com and identify the type of accommodation or assistance you are requesting. Do not include any medical or health information in this email. The Reasonable Accommodations team will respond to your email promptly.
Culture Amp will retain your CV & personal information for a period of two years (four years for the US) from the date of your application process completion. Culture Amp may contact you in relation to future job opportunities during this time period. For further information please see our privacy policy here or contact privacy@cultureamp.com.

jobs.title: Web Developer: WordPress & HubSpot (U.S. Based, Remote Contractor)
jobs.description:
SimpleTiger is hiring a part-time contract web developer to build, improve, and troubleshoot client websites in WordPress and HubSpot, with the potential to grow into a larger role.
We’re a B2B SaaS marketing agency helping software companies grow through SEO, content marketing, paid media, and answer engine optimization (AEO). Our clients’ websites are where much of that work comes to life, and we’re looking for a developer who can turn ideas into clean, functional pages quickly.
As part of our delivery team, you’ll work primarily on client websites, translating designs, campaign concepts, and SEO recommendations into effective web experiences. From building new pages to fixing issues on existing sites, you’ll help turn our marketing strategy into work that’s ready to launch.
Key responsibilities
- Build, update, or troubleshoot client websites in WordPress and HubSpot CMS
- Make technical fixes and improvements to live client sites, with clear details on what was tested, implemented, and performance comparisons using tools like Screaming Frog, pagespeed insights, and Lighthouse
- Build and connect forms, lead routing, and simple automations between a site and the client’s marketing tools
- Set up and check tracking, like GA4, Google Tag Manager, and HubSpot tracking in Tandem with the SEO Manager
- Keep sites fast, accessible, and friendly to SEO (page speed, Core Web Vitals, clean markup, image optimizations, cache lifetime improvements, and so on)
- Write clear and timely notes on what you are actively working on, and any updates pushed live so our team and the client can follow along
Qualifications and skills
- You’re a hands-on developer who can build from scratch, troubleshoot existing sites, and make improvements without disrupting what’s already working.
Required skills
- WordPress development: Strong experience with custom themes, child themes, blocks, page builders, and Advanced Custom Fields (ACF). You can build a page from the ground up—not just edit an existing one.
- HubSpot CMS development: Strong experience with HubL templates, modules, and themes, including building and troubleshooting pages, forms, and email templates.
- Front-end development: Solid HTML, CSS, and JavaScript skills, with the ability to navigate existing code and understand how changes affect the live site.
- APIs and integrations: Experience working with the HubSpot or WordPress REST APIs, plus CRMs and marketing tools such as Salesforce, Zapier, n8n, Airtable, and Slack.
- Technical audits and fixes: Experience using Screaming Frog to audit WordPress and HubSpot sites, interpret findings, and resolve technical issues.
- Code review and cleanup: Comfort working within WordPress and HubSpot codebases to identify legacy or unused JavaScript and CSS, determine what’s still needed, and safely remove what isn’t.
- Async communication: Clear, timely written communication, especially through Slack.
- Independent work: Strong time management and the ability to meet deadlines, flag blockers early, and keep projects moving without close supervision.
Nice-to-have skills
- Webflow development and auditing experience, including building a clean CMS structure.
- PHP development experience.
- Previous work at a marketing agency or with B2B SaaS clients.
- Familiarity with SEO and conversion best practices.
- Experience with Git and version control.
What success looks like
Success means delivering clean, reliable development work that helps our team turn marketing plans into live client experiences.
- Designs, campaign concepts, and SEO requests become functional pages in WordPress and HubSpot.
- Technical audit findings lead to practical fixes, with changes tested to avoid breaking existing functionality.
- Legacy and unused code is cleaned up thoughtfully, while essential code and front-end behavior remain intact.
- Forms, templates, and integrations work as intended and support the client’s marketing workflows.
- Projects stay on track because you manage your workload, meet agreed deadlines, and raise questions or blockers early.
- Teammates have clear visibility into progress through timely updates and straightforward communication in Slack.

jobs.title: Sr. Backend Engineer II - US Stocks
jobs.description:
Founded to transform retail finance, Ajaib Group is an Indonesian fintech unicorn breaking barriers to financial access. Having recently secured a $270M Series C—the single largest funding round in Southeast Asia over the past four years—we are backed by premier global investors including Y Combinator, Ribbit Capital, SoftBank, and SBI Holdings.
To build world-class products, we assemble world-class talent. Supported by our fully remote work arrangement, our team spans Eastern Europe, the Middle East, India, and Southeast Asia, allowing you to work with brilliant engineers and builders from around the globe from wherever you are. We operate with an impact-driven purpose where everyone is the owner of our customers' satisfaction. Driven by a growth mindset and a fierce will to win, we refuse to settle and constantly push engineering boundaries.
Role Overview
As a Sr. Backend Engineer II in the US Stocks team, you own backend services for trading US stocks from design to production: order flow to our brokerage partners, balances and currency conversion, market data, portfolio and corporate actions. You take on larger and more complex features, make sound design decisions under real traffic, and mentor engineers around you.
- Design, build and run scalable, secure backend services and APIs for trading, funding, market data and portfolio features.
- Own larger features and services end to end, including monitoring, alerting and on-call follow-up.
- Design for correctness first: accurate money and quantity handling, idempotent requests, safe retries and audit trails.
- Integrate with US brokerage and custody partners, and make those integrations resilient to outages, delays and duplicate or out-of-order messages.
- Build and improve reconciliation between our records and our partners' records, and drive root-cause fixes for mismatches.
- Handle US-specific events correctly, such as market hours, dividends, stock splits and settlement timing.
- Keep services fast and stable at US market open and during volatile days, and plan capacity ahead of known events.
- Lead design reviews and give thoughtful code reviews.
- Investigate production incidents, run root cause analysis and ship lasting fixes.
- Mentor mid-level engineers and share knowledge within the team.
- Design resilient, low-latency order routing logic to manage execution across multiple Liquidity Providers (LPs) and venues, handling rate limits, partial fills, and complex order lifecycles.
- Proactively identify systemic risks across the US Stocks domain and propose architectural improvements, acting as a technical bridge to Staff engineers.
Requirements
- Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.
- Experience: 5+ years of professional backend engineering, with a track record of owning production services under high traffic.
- Languages: Strong in Java, Go or another modern backend language.
- System Design: Solid understanding of microservices, REST/gRPC APIs, event-driven design, and reliability and observability practices.
- Data & Messaging: Hands-on with relational and NoSQL databases (query tuning), caching (Redis) and messaging (Kafka).
- Infrastructure: Experience running services on cloud platforms (GCP or AWS), with containers and CI/CD.
- Mindset & Domain: Ownership mindset and clear communication. Experience in brokerage, trading, payments, cross-border money movement or another regulated environment is a strong plus.
- Deep understanding of modern API-first brokerage platforms (e.g., Alpaca, Interactive Brokers) or crypto exchanges, including WebSocket streaming for market data and FIX protocol fundamentals.
Benefits
- Performance Bonus - Get rewarded for the impact you make
- Private Insurance - Comprehensive health coverage for you
- Paid Time Off - Take the time you need to recharge and come back stronger
- Learning & Development - Company-sponsored training, courses, and professional certifications
- Hybrid Work Arrangement - Enjoy the flexibility of working both remotely and from the office
- Career Growth - Work closely with experienced leaders and take on meaningful ownership as we scale
- Employee Perks - Enjoy exclusive discounts, partnerships, and lifestyle perks
- Collaborative & High-Ownership Culture - Work with smart, driven people in cross-functional teams, take ownership, and make a meaningful impact for our users.

jobs.description:
About BTSE:
BTSE Group is a global leader in fintech and blockchain technology, anchored by three core business pillars: Exchange, Payments, and Infrastructure Development. About the Opportunity:
We are seeking a Cyber Security Operations Center (CSOC) Analyst with 3-4 years of experience in security monitoring, detection engineering, and incident response to join a lean, high-ownership security team at a cryptocurrency exchange. You will work closely with our MSSP and internal engineering team to close gaps between raw alerting and actual risk reduction — turning threat intel feeds into action, validating that our detections actually work, and helping build out new programs like insider threat monitoring. This is not a pure alert-queue role: you'll be expected to write and improve detection logic, document your work so it survives beyond you, and take ownership of incidents end-to-end rather than handing off after triage.
Responsibilities:
- Perform triage, analysis, and escalation of security alerts across SIEM, EDR/XDR, WAF, email security, and cloud log sources, coordinating with our MSSP where relevant.
- Own incidents end-to-end — triage through resolution through "what changed afterward" — and turn that work into documented playbooks and updated detection logic, not just closed tickets.
- Develop, tune, and validate SIEM detection rules (ES|QL/EQL/KQL or equivalent), including running detection validation exercises against existing use cases to confirm they actually fire.
- Convert threat intelligence feeds and scheduled hunting queries (e.g., lookalike domain alerts, anomalous auth events) from passive detection into defined, actionable response — closing the loop between "we saw it" and "we did something about it."
- Support the build-out of an insider threat monitoring program, including identity and privileged-access anomaly detection.
- Understand our detection tooling and log source pipelines (maintained day-to-day by our MSSP) well enough to confirm they're onboarded correctly and actually working — you're not expected to build or maintain this tooling yourself, but you need to be able to verify it.
- Track and report CSOC performance metrics (MTTD/MTTR, false-positive rates, MSSP SLA adherence) to support continuous improvement of operations.
- Write and maintain operational documentation, playbooks, and detection rule rationale so institutional knowledge isn't concentrated in one or two people.
- Contribute to automation of repetitive triage and enrichment work (scripting, workflow tools) to reduce manual toil across the team.
- Collaborate with internal stakeholders and regional partners, where Chinese language skills may be required.
Requirements:
- Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field.
- 3-4 years of experience in a Security Operations Center (SOC) or equivalent security monitoring/detection engineering role.
- Hands-on experience with SIEM tools, including: 1. Detection rule and use case development, and the ability to reason about whether a rule actually detects what it claims to (detection validation mindset, not just rule-writing). 2. Query/rule-writing experience in ES|QL, EQL, KQL, or equivalent. 3. Alert triage, enrichment, and case management with ticketing systems. 4. Comfort reading raw logs (auth events, CloudTrail-style audit logs, process trees) without relying solely on pre-built dashboards.
- Working knowledge of Python or similar scripting for automation, log parsing, or extending existing tooling — enough to pick up and modify scripts someone else wrote, not build from scratch.
- Knowledge of common attack techniques, malware behavior, and network security principles, with familiarity mapping detections to MITRE ATT&CK.
- Familiarity with incident response frameworks (e.g., NIST, SANS) and a track record of writing playbooks or documentation from real incidents.
- Exposure to identity/IAM log analysis or insider threat / UEBA concepts is a strong plus, given active program build-out.
- Good understanding of cloud security (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and comfort across varied operating systems (Windows, Linux, macOS).
Nice to Haves
- Familiarity with atomic-level adversary emulation using Atomic Red Team or equivalent framework, for the purpose of validating that detections fire as expected.
- Effective communication and documentation skills.
- Chinese language proficiency (reading, writing, and/or speaking) is a strong advantage.
- Relevant certifications (e.g., CISSP, GCIH, GCFA, CompTIA Security+, CySA+, CEH, or similar) are desirable.
Perks & Benefits
- Competitive total compensation package.
- Various team-building programs and company events.
- And many more! Apply and let us tell you more!

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, (OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor)
jobs.description:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week
Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.
Check out this Loom video for more details:
We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.
This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.
What this role actually is
You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:
• Whether the response makes sense
- Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful
- Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment
- Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer
This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.
What you'll be doing
- Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end
- Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think
- Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code
- Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)
- Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading
- Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code
What we mean by "taste"
We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:
- Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?
- Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?
- Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?
- Would this interaction build or erode trust?
You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.
Who you are
- Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)
- Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python
- Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor
- Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows
- Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line
- Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement
- Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback
- High bar for what good engineering looks like
Nice to have
- Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows
- Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards
Engagement details
- Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location
• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible
- Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well
- Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat
- Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

jobs.description:
About KIRA
Our mission is to make money smart, reliable and within reach for everyone.
In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.
Today, we are expanding ways to help people in Asia and it includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and at ease and self reliance, become an expert. We believe AI will help us achieve this in our generation.
We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.
We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future.
If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.
The Role
KIRA builds technology products used by millions of users across Southeast Asia. As our products and systems scale, we need technical leaders who can solve difficult engineering problems and raise the engineering bar around them.
The Staff Software Engineer owns technical direction and execution for major products and systems. This is a hands-on role - you will design systems, write code, and drive critical engineering work from idea to production.
What You'll Own
- Owning technical design and execution for major products, systems and engineering initiatives.
- Designing scalable, reliable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.
- Building alongside the team through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.
- Driving architecture decisions and trade-offs across speed, scalability, reliability, cost and maintainability.
- Turning ambiguous product problems into clear technical solutions and execution plans.
- Raising engineering quality through stronger system design, testing, security, observability and development practices.
- Leading technically critical initiatives and mentoring engineers across teams.
What We're Looking For
- 7+ years of software engineering experience building and shipping production systems.
- Deep expertise in backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.
- Strong system design and architecture skills for complex or high-scale systems.
- Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.
- Track record of technically leading major engineering projects from design through production.
- Ability to make sound technical trade-offs, influence engineers and solve complex production problems.
Nice to have
- Experience scaling engineering teams, systems or development practices through significant growth.
- Experience operating across multiple products, markets or countries.
Location
This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.
Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.
Language
English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.
Interview Process
Our process is designed to move fast:
- Online assessment or practical task
- Technical interview
- CEO / final round
For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

jobs.title: Remote Python Senior Software Engineer, AI Training
jobs.description:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week
Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.
Check out this Loom video for more details:
We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.
This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.
What this role actually is
You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:
• Whether the response makes sense
- Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful
- Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment
- Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer
This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.
What you'll be doing
- Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end
- Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think
- Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code
- Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)
- Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading
- Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code
What we mean by "taste"
We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:
- Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?
- Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?
- Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?
- Would this interaction build or erode trust?
You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.
Who you are
- Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)
- Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python
- Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor
- Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows
- Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line
- Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement
- Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback
- High bar for what good engineering looks like
Nice to have
- Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows
- Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards
Engagement details
- Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location
• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible
- Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well
- Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat
- Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

jobs.title: Senior UX Designer
jobs.description:
Senior UX Designer
Location: Remote
Duration: Permanent
Hours: Full time
Summary
The Wikimedia Foundation is a non-profit organization supporting Wikipedia and other Wiki projects. The Foundation operates one of the world’s top five websites and has global reach and impact. Technology and innovation are critical in our quest to support every human in freely sharing knowledge.
The Product Design team is looking for a Senior UX Designer with a solid understanding of user experience and product development processes to work within a new multi-disciplinary product team that will be focused on improving trust and safety. You will be influential in creating and developing the user experience, feeding directly into the product strategy for your product team.
For this role, you will primarily be working with the Reader Growth team, software focused on ways of learning and engagement for new and casual readers of Wikipedia.
Must be available for design, product and engineering team meetings and synchronous collaboration from 14:00 UTC and 18:00 UTC (10:00-14:00 ET / 7:00-11:00 PT)
You will be responsible for…
- Reducing complexity to create simple, delightful experiences for our users.
- Creating prototypes and running experiments to iteratively test your hypotheses.
- Using and evolving our design system and guidelines, to create new features from ideas on paper to implementation.
- Applying accessibility standards and guidelines to your designs.
- Collaborating with product managers and engineers to create product plans and maintain product design processes.
- Distilling complex concepts into easy to understand talking points to engage with our readers and communities throughout the design process.
Skills and experience….
The right person is better than the right set of experiences. These are the traits we’ve identified that make great additions to our team so far.
- Can communicate their design goals and processes clearly and concisely to other team members and stakeholders.
- Provides constructive feedback to other designers and welcomes feedback from others.
- Experienced in conducting research, as well as collaborating with UX researchers, to build a deeper understanding of audience behaviours.
- Is able to generate ideas for the future as well as think tactically about how to deliver work in the present.
- Is self-motivated and seeks to evolve their skills and share what they’ve learnt with others.
- 5+ years of experience contributing on design teams.
- Bachelor's degree and/or Masters degree, or equivalent in related work experience
Additionally, we’d love it if you have...
- Background in content consumption, publishing, education, or news
- Experience acting as a researcher, both in-person and with remote participants
- Have familiarity with Free Knowledge and/or Open Source communities
- Speak more than one of the nearly 300 languages of the users you’ll be designing for
Team requirements
- Attendance of mandatory design team meetings weekly on:
- Mondays from 14:00-15:00 UTC (10:00-11:00 ET / 7:00-8:00 PT)
- Tuesdays from 14:30-16:00 UTC (10:30-12:00 ET / 7:30-9:00 PT)
- Thursdays from 14:00-15:30 UTC (10:00-11:30 ET / 7:00-8:30 PT)
- Availability for team meetings and synchronous collaboration with primary product team from 14:00 UTC and 18:00 UTC (10:00-14:00 ET / 7:00-11:00 PT)
About the Wikimedia Foundation
The Wikimedia Foundation is the nonprofit organization that operates Wikipedia and the other Wikimedia free knowledge projects. Our vision is a world in which every single human can freely share in the sum of all knowledge. We believe that everyone has the potential to contribute something to our shared knowledge, and that everyone should be able to access that knowledge freely. We host Wikipedia and the Wikimedia projects, build software experiences for reading, contributing, and sharing Wikimedia content, support the volunteer communities and partners who make Wikimedia possible, and advocate for policies that enable Wikimedia and free knowledge to thrive.
The Wikimedia Foundation is a charitable, not-for-profit organization that relies on donations. We receive donations from millions of individuals around the world, with an average donation of about $15. We also receive donations through institutional grants and gifts. The Wikimedia Foundation is a United States 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization with offices in San Francisco, California, USA.
As an equal opportunity employer, the Wikimedia Foundation values having a diverse workforce and continuously strives to maintain an inclusive and equitable workplace. We encourage people with a diverse range of backgrounds to apply. We do not discriminate against any person based upon their race, traits historically associated with race, religion, color, national origin, sex, pregnancy or related medical conditions, parental status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, or any other legally protected characteristics.
The Wikimedia Foundation is a remote-first organization with staff members including contractors based 40+ countries*. Salaries at the Wikimedia Foundation are set in a way that is competitive, equitable, and consistent with our values and culture. The anticipated annual pay range of this position for applicants based within the United States is US$116,633 to US$181,243 with multiple individualized factors, including cost of living in the location, being the determinants of the offered pay. For applicants located outside of the US, the pay range will be adjusted to the country of hire. We neither ask for nor take into consideration the salary history of applicants. The compensation for a successful applicant will be based on their skills, experience and location.
*Please note that we are currently able to hire in the following:
US States: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, District of Columbia*, Florida, Georgia, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Puerto Rico*, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, West Virginia, Wisconsin and Wyoming (*US Territory or Federal District)
Countries: Brazil, Canada, Colombia, France, Germany, Ghana, India, Indonesia, Italy, Kenya*, Mexico, Morocco, Netherlands, Poland, Singapore*, South Africa, Spain, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. Our non-US employees are hired through a local third party Employer of Record (EOR) and must have current work authorization in their location. (*citizens/permanent residents only)

All applicants can reach out to their recruiter to understand more about the specific pay range for their location during the interview process.

🫵 Role: Principal Data Analyst (Researcher)
📍 Location: Jakarta, Indonesia
✒️ Freelancing contract, 12 months duration
🕐 Possibility of conversion to a full-time position
📅 Deadline for applications: 31/10/2026, at midnight
Job Description
Do you have the drive and aptitude to turn ideas into reality? Do you share our passion for the environment and harnessing technology to decarbonize our society? Do you know or want to learn how environmental policy and politics can transform markets, and have an interest in sustainable transportation in Indonesia and your community? If you do, this may well be the job for you. We are seeking a Data Analyst for Indonesia. This is a role based in Indonesia, preferably Jakarta.
We are looking for a candidate who can develop and apply advanced quantitative analysis tools and techniques, synthesizing data from various sources to support our mission of creating a sustainable transport system. This could include for example total cost of ownership assessments, life-cycle analysis, and techno-economic feasibility research. The role will involve evaluating the reliability and relevance of evidence and providing objective, technical advice to shape policy and influence the public narrative on maritime (shipping) and/or road transport issues.
The ideal candidate will have a background in engineering, economics, or a related scientific field, with experience in transport and energy modeling, research, or similar areas. We are unfortunately only able to consider candidates with the unrestricted legal right to work in Indonesia. The salary package and title depend on an assessment of relevant experience.
Project Overview
This project is part of an effort to accelerate Indonesia's transition, supporting its economy-wide net zero emissions goal by 2060 or sooner. The focus is on the decarbonization of the transport sector with particular focus on the maritime and heavy duty vehicle sector.
Key Roles and Responsibilities
- Lead T&E’s analytical and research in maritime (shipping) and trucking work for Indonesia.
- Deliver economic/energy/transport modelling and/or analysis on the impacts of national and/or regional transport policy.
- Commission research and collaborate with T&E's partners in the region, ensuring that T&E’s quality standards are upheld in all deliverables.
- Write technical reports and policy briefings that detail these impacts and the policy changes that would help deliver them.
- Present research findings internally and externally.
- Develop compelling, high quality and narrative driven graphs and data visualizations with Flourish and other interactive tools (such as netlify).
- Support T&E’s analytical work in other work programmes when additional capacity is required.
- Review T&E analytical outputs to ensure a high degree of research, analysis, and argumentation. This includes quality-assuring models, challenging input data and assumptions and interpreting output data.
- Provide input to T&E’s policy and communication strategies.
- Promote informed discussion on contemporary transport debates among T&E analysts and across the organization.
- Network with communities of transport analysts to ensure a two-way flow of relevant findings
Job requirements:
- 5+ years relevant or equivalent professional experience in transport economics/analysis, climate/energy analysis or transport policy.
- Experience or expertise in detailed quantitative analysis such as economic or transport modelling, data science or regression analysis is required. Expertise in programming (for example leveraging Python with AI tools) and/or qualitative analysis (e.g. interviews, surveys, literature reviews, content analysis) are considered a bonus.
- Excellent communication and presentation skills and an ability to write in English fluently, accurately and concisely. Other relevant languages are considered a bonus.
- Project management experience including strong interpersonal and team-working skills and an ability to deliver to tight deadlines.
- The confidence to think and act with initiative, to engage and influence policymakers, industry representatives and other stakeholders at the highest level.
Contract Duration, Location, Remuneration
- Duration: This is a one-year consultancy contract, with a high possibility of conversion to a full-time position upon successful completion of the term and depending on future project needs.
- Work Arrangement: [e.g., Consultant Contract/Flexible arrangement, including required travel for meetings/data gathering.
- The salary package and title depends on experience. We are an equal opportunities employer and offer competitive salary and benefits.
About T&E
T&E is the independent expert in enabling clean transport for all. Our vision is a zero-emissions mobility system that is affordable and has minimal impacts on our health and environment. Since we were created 30 years ago, T&E has shaped some of Europe’s most important environmental laws. We got the EU to set the world's most ambitious CO2 standards for cars and trucks but also helped uncover the Dieselgate scandal; we campaigned successfully to end palm oil diesel, secured a global ban on dirty shipping fuels and the creation of the aviation ETS, the world's largest carbon market for aviation, to name just a few.
We combine the power of robust, science-based evidence and a deep understanding of transport with powerful communications and impactful advocacy. Our staff in Brussels, Paris, Rome, Madrid, Berlin, Warsaw and London collaborate with our 49 national members. From 2024, T&E has been enhancing our collaboration between Asia and Europe, starting from our Singapore office, to accelerate zero-emission transport and energy transition, helping ensure that global decarbonization efforts are both inclusive and regionally grounded. Altogether, our members represent more than 3.5 million people.

jobs.title: Software Engineer - Console
jobs.description:
About XBOW
Build the future of offensive security with XBOW. Attackers are already using AI to move faster than defenders can react—we’re creating the platform that puts security ahead in the arms race. Our AI-powered system autonomously discovers, validates, and even exploits vulnerabilities, giving organizations proof-backed results in hours instead of weeks.
Founded by Oege de Moor, creator of GitHub Copilot, and backed by Sequoia, Altimeter, and other leading investors, XBOW is applying cutting-edge AI to one of the world’s most urgent problems. In just over a year, our AI, built by a world-class AI team and legendary security researchers — has uncovered thousands of real-world zero-days across the software billions rely on, and achieved the #1 ranking on HackerOne’s global leaderboard.
We’re a team of builders, hackers, and researchers who thrive on solving problems others think are impossible. If you want to push the boundaries of AI, reshape how security is done, and join the group defining this new era of defense — we’d love to talk.
Your Role
We’re looking for a Software Engineer who’s passionate about building reliable and high quality products with robust backend systems. In this role, you’ll design and implement end-to-end features across the stack: from React-based frontends and TypeScript APIs to backend services in Kotlin and Go, all deployed on AWS.
You’ll be joining a small team of superstars that’s shipping quickly and operating with high trust. This is a role for someone who loves to own open-ended problems and figure things out—whether that’s designing seamless API contracts, optimizing database interactions, or building scalable systems that make powerful AI capabilities accessible. If you like being at the intersection of deep tech and real-world impact, you’ll feel right at home.
What You'll Do
-
Design and build full-stack systems that integrate frontend and backend seamlessly
-
Develop scalable APIs and backend services in TypeScript, Kotlin, and Go
-
Deploy and operate services in AWS and other cloud providers
-
Own problems end-to-end—from design through deployment to production support
-
Navigate ambiguity and help define how we build as much as what we build
-
Collaborate closely with teammates across the stack, including AI researchers, Security researchers and backend engineers
Who You Are
-
Experience building and operating full-stack systems
-
Proficiency with TypeScript
-
Experience designing and consuming APIs (REST or GraphQL)
-
Strong backend development experience (Node.js, Kotlin, Go, or similar languages)
-
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work with incomplete information
-
A thoughtful communicator who values clarity and simplicity
-
Comfort working in a fast-paced, early-stage startup environment
Bonus If You Have
-
Experience with event-driven architectures, message queues, or async workflows
-
Experience building scrappy, iterative frontends where speed and feedback loops matter more than polish
-
Familiarity with AWS or similar cloud platforms
-
Comfort working with infrastructure as code (e.g., Terraform or CDK)
-
A strong appreciation for user experience and design, even if you’re not a formal designer — you care about how features feel as much as how they work
-
Comfortable prototyping quickly in React/TypeScript and turning ideas into working features fast
-
Experience designing and optimizing relational databases (we use Postgres), and you know how to structure data for both performance and clarity.
-
Background in systems programming, networking, or performance tuning
-
Experience with hybrid deployments (cloud + on-prem) and know how to build resilient systems that handle the complexity of mixed environments.
-
Experience working in an early stage startup
-
Prior experience building security products or products for technical users
What We Offer
-
Compensation & Equity: Competitive salary and a generous equity package, making you a true owner of the company.
-
Career Growth: Shape your role, lead the function, and grow with the company as we redefine cybersecurity.
-
Meaningful Work: You will tackle technically complex challenges and play a pivotal role in the growth of our business, working alongside an amazing team and some of the world’s experts to shape how AI transforms cybersecurity.
What Else You Should Know
-
Location: Remote (all team members are remote but we meet regularly and you’re supported to travel to collaborate with colleagues in person)
-
Contract: Full-time.
-
Hiring Process:
-
45-min introductory chat with our Talent team.
-
45 minutes with one of our Engineering Leads.
-
2-3 hour technical deep dive around relevant case study.

30-min final meeting with the Engineering Lead for the assigned team..

We believe in people who are driven by curiosity and a willingness to learn. Even if you don't check every box, we encourage you to apply if you're excited about the role and our mission.

At Cloudbeds, we're not just building software, we're transforming hospitality. Our platform powers hotels across 150 countries, processing billions in bookings annually. This is a product engineering role focused on production AI systems, agentic workflows, evaluation, and observability - not an internal tooling role. You'll work primarily in Python while collaborating across our broader PHP and Java ecosystem, building systems where correctness, reliability, latency, cost, and model quality are core to the job. The Core AI Squad owns the customer-facing AI platform infrastructure, agentic workflows, and evaluation and observability foundations that enable AI-powered experiences across Cloudbeds products. The team builds the production capabilities that let us evaluate models and providers for specific use cases, orchestrate tools and workflows, measure quality over time, and integrate AI safely into real customer journeys. Architect and implement MCP (Model Context Protocol) integrations that allow AI agents to interact with business systems contextually and safely — enabling intelligent, event-driven actions across the GTM platform.

Explore and evaluate emerging AI capabilities (RAG, fine-tuning, multi-agent orchestration) and determine which are production-ready for GTM business systems use cases.
-
Build reusable AI templates, automation patterns, and agent blueprints that can be extended across the GTM Engineering team.
Business Systems Integration & Architecture
-
Build and maintain integrations across Salesforce, NetSuite, Workato, MuleSoft, DealHub (CPQ), and other GTM platforms — with a strong bias toward clean architecture, low technical debt, and supportable design.
-
Own end-to-end integration patterns for critical business flows such as lead-to-opportunity, quote-to-cash, order-to-fulfillment, and revenue reporting pipelines.
-
Design data flows and transformation logic that keep business data accurate, consistent, and accessible across systems without creating fragile point-to-point dependencies.
-
Apply a build-vs-buy mindset: evaluate whether a given automation need is best solved with native platform capabilities, iPaaS tooling, or custom code — and make the case clearly.
Platform Development & Tooling
-
Build internal tooling, low-code/no-code solutions, and lightweight applications using platforms such as Retool, Replit, or similar to extend business systems capabilities with minimal overhead.
-
Write automation scripts and data transformation logic in Python, JavaScript, or Apex as needed to bridge gaps that platform tooling cannot address natively.
-
Utilize Zapier, Workato, and similar iPaaS platforms to orchestrate cross-system workflows that are maintainable, observable, and well-documented.
-
Own the full lifecycle of what you build: discovery, design, development, testing, deployment, documentation, and ongoing optimization.
Reliability, Observability & Continuous Improvement
-
Monitor the health and performance of automations and integrations you own; proactively identify degradation, data inconsistencies, or failure patterns before they impact business operations.
-
Conduct root-cause analysis of integration failures or automation breakdowns and drive durable fixes — not just incident patches.
-
Maintain runbooks and operational documentation so that platform behavior is understandable and recoverable by the broader team.
-
Gather feedback from business stakeholders and iterate on existing automations to improve accuracy, reduce edge cases, and adapt to evolving GTM processes.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement
-
Partner with Sales, Revenue Operations, Finance, and Customer Success stakeholders to translate business requirements into well-scoped technical solutions.
-
Work closely with GTM Systems Engineering, DevOps, and BSA teammates on architecture decisions, intake prioritization, and delivery execution.
-
Contribute to the GTM Systems Engineering operating model: maintain task hygiene, communicate proactively on large initiatives, and log AI/automation work in the team's AI Excellence registry.
-
Serve as a subject matter expert for business systems automation and AI — educating stakeholders on what's possible and setting realistic expectations on scope and delivery.
Qualifications
Experience
-
3–5+ years in a business systems engineering, systems administration, or integration engineering role.
-
Demonstrated experience building and shipping automations or integrations that delivered measurable business value in production environments.
-
Hands-on experience with Salesforce and at least one ERP platform (NetSuite strongly preferred).
-
Experience deploying AI or LLM-powered automations in a production business systems context — or a clear, demonstrated trajectory toward it.
-
Experience working in a high-velocity environment where you manage multiple concurrent priorities and adapt quickly to changing business needs.
-
Optional but valued: experience with DealHub (CPQ), ClickUp, quote-to-cash workflows, or revenue operations systems.
Skills & Competencies
Technical
-
Salesforce configuration, automation (Flow, Process Builder), Apex, and data model design — admin or developer-level proficiency required.
-
NetSuite workflows, SuiteScript, SuiteBundler, saved searches, and data model — particularly as it relates to order management, billing, and revenue recognition.
-
Hands-on experience with Workato, MuleSoft, Zapier, or comparable iPaaS platforms — including multi-step flows, error handling, and observability.
-
Practical experience with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Claude, etc.), prompt engineering, agentic workflow design, and MCP integrations. Experience with ClickUp Super Agents is a strong plus.
-
Proficient with Python, JavaScript, or Apex for automation scripting and data transformation; comfortable with REST APIs, webhooks, JSON, and OAuth-based integrations.
-
Strong understanding of business systems data models and integration patterns (event-driven, batch, real-time).
Operational & Mindset
-
Ownership: You take full responsibility for the systems you build — from reliability and documentation to stakeholder trust and continuous improvement. You don't hand off and walk away.
-
Velocity: You move fast, iterate, and ship. You know when "good enough and deployed" beats "perfect and blocked," and you never sacrifice reliability or data integrity to get there.
-
AI & Automation mindset: You default to asking "how can an agent or LLM handle this?" before reaching for a manual workflow — experimenting confidently and evaluating critically.
-
Collaboration: You bridge the gap between technical architecture and business impact, asking clarifying questions, challenging assumptions respectfully, and earning trust with the stakeholders you support.
-
Growth: You stay current on emerging AI capabilities, evaluate what's production-ready, and continuously raise the bar on what GTM systems can do.
What You'll Work With

Salesforce: CRM platform — automations, Flow, Apex, data model, reporting, and CPQ/OTC integrations.

NetSuite: ERP platform — SuiteScript, workflows, order management, billing, and revenue recognition flows.

ClickUp Super Agents: AI-powered automation and agentic task orchestration within the ClickUp ecosystem.

Low-code tooling: Retool, Replit, or similar for internal applications and workflow extensions.

Scripting & APIs: Python, JavaScript, Apex, REST/webhook integrations, and JSON-based data transformation.
